An 11-year-old girl from London has become the first patient in the UK to receive a groundbreaking gene therapy for a rare condition that progressively robs children of their sight.

Catherine L’Estrange, from North Acton, underwent the innovative treatment, which involves injecting healthy copies of a specific gene directly into the eye.

This pioneering procedure had only been performed on one other individual globally prior to Catherine’s operation.

Diagnosed with Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) as a baby, Catherine is hopeful the therapy will enable her to continue her beloved hobby of reading.

According to her surgeon, if successful, the treatment could stabilise her vision or even lead to an improvement.

BBS is caused by mutations in one of 20 different genes, affecting approximately one in 100,000 births in the UK. Patients typically experience blindness by their late teens or early twenties.

Beyond vision loss, the condition can also manifest with kidney problems, learning difficulties, obesity, and occasionally extra fingers or toes.

The hour-long procedure, utilising gene therapy developed by biotechnology company MeiraGTx, was carried out at St Helier Hospital in March.

Surgeons removed the jelly inside her eye and injected healthy copies of a gene into the retina, the light sensitive layer of tissue at the back of the eye.

open image in gallery Catherine was diagnosed with Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) as a baby ( Family handout )

In people with BBS, small cells in the retina die, leading to blindness.

Neruban Kumaran, consultant eye surgeon at Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust, told the Press Association: “By giving a healthy copy of the gene, it helps save those cells, and the hope is to either stabilise or improve vision.”

Catherine said: “If this treatment works, it will help me to carry on seeing things around me, and most of all I will be able to carry on reading books, which is one of my favourite things to do.”

Her father, Reverend Timothy L’Estrange, said most children with BBS do not get diagnosed until they are in primary school, but Catherine was diagnosed at a few weeks old, allowing the family to plan her future.

“Our policy was to develop her independence and resilience as much as possible, ready for the inevitable loss of her sight, which began with her becoming night-blind, then colour-blind, and continued with her losing her peripheral vision,” he said.

“We were told that possible gene therapy was many, many years away, and was likely to arrive after Catherine had entirely lost her sight – so we were surprised and delighted when we learned this treatment had become available, and that Catherine would be one of the first patients in the world to receive it.”

open image in gallery Catherine L'Estrange with her father, Timothy ( Family handout )

Just one of Catherine’s eyes has been treated with the new gene therapy, with the team now waiting to see the results.

The treatment is designed specifically for patients with a BBS10 gene mutation, which is one of the most common among BBS patients.

The team at St Helier worked with experts at Great Ormond Street and Moorfields Eye Hospital to identify eligible patients, as youngsters with BBS have genetic tests to pinpoint which of the 20 genes is mutated based on their symptoms.

Only one other person – a 17-year-old girl from Canada – had received the treatment before Catherine.

Her procedure took place at St Helier in August last year.

The parents of the girl, who wishes to remain anonymous, said: “This treatment has given our daughter a precious chance to preserve her vision, and we hope it will become a life-changing therapy for children with BBS10 all over the world.”

Since Catherine, the procedure has also been performed on one other younger child with BBS.

After having the therapy, patients are seen in clinic and have various sight tests, such as reading from a chart and identifying different shades of colours.

Mr Kumaran said some have already said their vision is better in dim light and the feedback so far has been positive, though it will take years before the full results are known.

“There is a hope that it may improve vision slightly, but it’s difficult to say,” he told PA.

“It’s not going to leave someone with perfect vision. But the hope is to stabilise and/or improve vision. Only time will tell.

“There’s been some very positive feedback from a mixture of the patients and the families that suggest their vision may be better.

open image in gallery Just one of Catherine’s eyes has been treated with the new gene therapy, with the team now waiting to see the results ( Family handout )

“Early reports from the families have been very promising, and it gives us lots of hope. But in practice, it will take many years before we’re sure.”

Reverend L’Estrange said: “Our whole family has been so grateful for the opportunity to save Catherine’s vision – it will be absolutely life-changing for her to retain any vision at all.”

Mr Kumaran is hopeful there will be other children out there eligible for the therapy, as well as babies who have not even been born yet.

He told PA it has been a “real honour” to have the opportunity to help these children, adding: “These families and the children have a lot of difficulties as it is, just because of all the other conditions they’re affected by.

“And one of the things that causes a lot of anxiety is the worry that these children lose vision and possibly lose their independence.

“There’s no other treatment for this, and so the opportunity to protect vision or improve vision, or give them hope that they won’t lose their vision and they can maintain that independence, it really means a lot.”

Mat Shaw, chief executive of St George’s, Epsom and St Helier Hospitals Group, said: “As a father, I can’t imagine how it feels to watch your child slowly go blind, and I’m so proud that our teams are offering hope to these children and their families, which aims to stop childhood blindness in its tracks and change what’s possible for the future of children with this devastating condition.”

UK defence spending "falls well short" of what is required to protect the country, the chief executive of BAE Systems has warned.

Charles Woodburn described the current climate as “the most threatening time I’ve seen” and warned Russia's military advances before and during its war with Ukraine were a key concern.

Despite the government announcing an additional £15 billion for defence in June, the then-defence secretary John Healey resigned, citing inadequate military funding.

At the time, Mr Healey wrote to Sir Keir Starmer to say he had been “unable, and the Treasury has been unwilling, to commit the resources that the nation needs to defend the country at this time of rising threats”.

Mr Woodburn said the extra funding still “falls well short of what is needed to protect the country”.

“This is by far the most threatening time I’ve seen,” he told the BBC. “Even when I joined the company in 2016, I was amazed at what we saw Russian submarines doing, the cyber attacks.

“I think that’s come a long way sadly as a result of the Ukraine conflict; we’re much more aware of the proximity of a hot war in Europe.”

Sir Keir Starmer speaks with Charles Woodburn from BAE Systems ( AFP/Getty )

He said modern warfare had “changed quite profoundly” and described Russia and Ukraine as becoming “incredibly adept” at the use of drones and counter-drones.

“It’s something that we now have to really understand and make sure that we’re able to provide the capabilities that can counter that and deter aggression,” he said.

It comes after Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the government of “complicity in the crime of aggression and war crimes” by allowing the US to carry out “unlawful attacks”.

While the government has refused to take part in offensive campaigns against Iran, it has allowed the US to launch defensive strikes from British bases hosting American personnel. Prime minister Andy Burnham has maintained Sir Keir Starmer’s agreement to allow the US to use British bases, including RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire.

Junior housing minister Sally Jameson backed the new prime minister’s decision on Friday, insisting the government “will always act within the best interests of our national security and the interests of the British people”.

“I think that's the right position for the moment because the British government always makes sure that our interests are protected, our defences are protected, and that British citizens that are living abroad and living in that region are kept safe,” she told Sky News.

Shares in BAE Systems rose by 3.25 per cent, with other defence companies also seeing a rise following the appointment of Mr Healey as chancellor on Monday, with expectations he will commit to further defence spending.

“The fact that he understands the requirements of defence we see as a very positive thing,” Mr Woodburn said.

BAE Systems announced this week the Ministry of Defence has given it a contract extension worth £708 million to continue developing a next-generation combat aircraft.

New defence secretary Wes Streeting said: “This investment in advanced combat air technology for the UK Armed Forces will strengthen our defence and deterrence, and shows our clear commitment to backing British workers with our defence investment, creating jobs and supporting communities across the UK.”

Consumer confidence has seen a significant six-point 'Burnham bounce', the largest increase since November 2023.

GfK suggests heatwaves, football success, and a new Prime Minister have 'lifted the mood', though the headline figure remains firmly negative at minus 17.

Confidence in the country’s general economic situation over the last 12 months jumped by 10 points to minus 39 – five points higher than a year ago.

Expectations for the economy over the coming 12 months also rose by eight points to minus 28 – one point above July 2025.

The Major Purchase Index, indicating big-ticket item confidence, increased eight points to minus 12, three points higher than last July.

Personal finances for the next year climbed three points into positive territory at one, though one point lower than last July.

The survey was taken between July 1 and July 14, ahead of Mr Burnham walking into Number 10 on July 20 and making any policy announcements.

The World Cup helped to boost confidence in the UK economy ( PA )

Neil Bellamy, consumer insights director at GfK, said: “Hot on the heels of the summer heatwaves, July has delivered a wave of optimism.

“The sense of a fresh start following the appointment of a new Prime Minister surely accounts for some of this bounce.

“There were also hopes at the start of July that the Middle East conflict might stabilise and bring UK fuel prices down.

“The feel-good factor of the Fifa World Cup will have reinforced sentiment too.

“However, July’s improved Overall Index Score remains within the narrow range seen since the end of 2023, and it is a decade since the headline score was in positive territory.

“For the ‘Burnham bounce’ to be sustainable and boost consumer confidence, it will require consistent delivery by the refreshed UK Government against deep cost-of-living challenges and persistent low economic growth.”

Burnham’s policy pledges

Mr Burnham has begun his premiership with a clear focus on alleviating the financial strain on households, rolling out a series of policy pledges in his inaugural week.

Addressing his newly assembled cabinet for the first time on Tuesday, the Prime Minister declared his administration would be a "cost of living government".

This commitment was swiftly followed by several announcements aimed at easing the financial burden on people across the country.

Mr Burnham’s ambitious vision was first articulated in his inaugural speech on Monday, where he vowed to dismantle economic policies introduced by the Thatcher administration in the 1980s.

He promised to usher in "the biggest changes in the last 40 years," signalling a significant shift in national direction.

US president Donald Trump’s latest tariffs are not set to see further changes for UK firms, but there are fears British exporters could lose out after the EU secured a more favourable trade deal.

The plans have seen America hit 60 countries including the UK with trade tariffs of between 10% and 12.5% over forced labour concerns.

The US trade department said the tariffs are being imposed on countries it claims have not taken action to tackle the importing of goods made with forced labour.

They are being introduced to replace temporary 10% levies as they came to an end on Friday, having been declared illegal by the US supreme court in February.

Expert William Bain, head of trade policy at the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC), said while it would be “business as usual” for most British firms exporting to the US, the UK must continue negotiating with the US over tariffs.

There are worries that the UK could become less competitive as US imports from other countries will be treated differently under the new regime.

The US has also threatened tariffs on imports from the UK and Europe that introduce digital services taxes, with Britain having said it will impose a 2% levy on the revenue of big tech firms.

Mr Bain said: “There will be concerns about the loss of the UK’s competitive advantage over the EU and other countries which have secured a more favourable deal in other goods sectors.

“The US is also carrying our further investigations over digital service taxes which could lead to further uncertainty for firms.

“It is crucial that the UK continues negotiations to ensure our companies have the best possible long-term trading terms with the US.

“Expanding our goods and services exports is vital to the UK’s economic growth and the US is our largest single country trading partner.”

He added: “This is unlikely to be the end of the story on US tariffs for either the UK or the rest of the world.

“The Government will need to keep a close eye on developments to keep the UK at the front of the pack.”

Simon Geale, executive vice president at procurement and supply chain consultancy Proxima, said UK companies risk being “caught off-guard” by the new tariffs.

He said: “The measures could lead to increased costs, inflation, and reduced domestic competition.

“Businesses need to move rapidly to prepare themselves, as the winners will likely be those who can adapt to new trading relationships.”

The GMB trade union blasted America’s new tariffs as “ill-judged, potentially catastrophic for business and likely to utterly fail in their stated aim”.

Charlotte Brumpton-Childs, GMB national secretary, said: “Despite claiming they have been introduced to prevent forced labour, in fact they will lead to job losses and reduced earnings for workers across the world.

“The EU now has a better trading relationship with the US than we do – which undermines the so-called ‘special relationship’.

“Once again, the president’s knee-jerk actions will gain nothing, hurt US business and take dollars out of people’s pockets.”

Jurgen Klopp will make his return to management for the first time since leaving Liverpool as the new head coach of the Germany national team, it has been confirmed.

Klopp cited fatigue when he left Liverpool in 2024 but said he is now “recharged”. The 59-year-old has been appointed in the aftermath of Germany’s disappointing World Cup campaign, which saw them exit at the last-32 stage following a penalty shootout defeat to Paraguay.

Given the manner of their exit, former coach Julian Nagelsmann was asked to resign by the German football association DFB who then pursued talks with Klopp to become the next head coach.

“The national team brings us Germans together like almost nothing else can. That's what makes this task so special for me,” Klopp said at his unveiling in Frankfurt on Friday morning.

open image in gallery Jurgen Klopp during a press conference with DFB President Bernd Neuendorf and Vice President Hans-Joachim Watzke ( Reuters )

The DFB announced that Klopp had reached “an agreement on the key points” of a deal to take over the national team on Saturday 11 July, following talks in New York, with a four-year contract up to the 2030 World Cup now signed.

Klopp managed Liverpool for nine years taking charge in October 2015 before departing at the end of the 2024 season having won both the Premier League and Champions League with the Reds

His most recent role was as Red Bull's Head of Global Soccer, a position he held since January 2025, overseeing Red Bull's network of clubs—including RB Leipzig, Red Bull Salzburg, and the New York Red Bulls.

Most recently he has been working as a pundit during the World Cup in the USA, Mexico and Canada and created headlines by suggesting that Deniz Undav should start ahead of Jamal Musiala and then saying that “Julian Nagelsmann is still picking the team – for now.”

Klopp was called out over the “for now” comment by former German players and apologised saying he felt like “punching himself in the face”.

Following these incidents and ahead of Nagelsmann’s resignation, the 59-year-old played coy about the prospect of replacing him by saying: “I understand that when the national coach position is discussed, my name is mentioned in some form but it's not the moment to really talk about it.”

Klopp’s national team ambitions were well known during the World Cup and his contract with Red Bull included a special exit clause designed specifically so that he could take on the Germany job should it become available.

News.title: Africa improves health defences, but it remains vulnerable to pandemics
News.content:
Africa is significantly better prepared for a pandemic than it was five years ago, a major review of the continent’s health security has found.

The review, which tracked dozens of health metrics across the continent, found that local and international investments in Africa’s health sector since the pandemic have “paid off.”

Published by the Brown University Pandemic Centre and the Nuclear Threat Initiative, a US non-profit, the report is the third of its kind and provides an update on two previous reviews from 2019 and 2021.

Investment in health by African governments grew rapidly during the pandemic. Post-pandemic, the average spend now sits at around 7.4 per cent of GDP, roughly $135 billion per year across the continent.

That figure still falls significantly below those of high-income countries, where the average spend on health sits at around 11.2 per cent of GDP.

The new African Health Security Index report found that almost every African country – 53 out of 54, excluding only the Republic of the Congo – has improved its ability to prevent, detect, and respond to disease outbreaks since 2021, the last time the index was updated.

Overall, the continent scores 41.2 out of 100 on its health security – up from 32.9 five years ago.

The score is built from hundreds of specific indicators covering things like how far people live from a hospital, how well infectious patients can be isolated, the size and training level of the health workforce, laboratory capacity, and the availability of vaccines and other critical medicines during an outbreak.

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

Sports.title: Arsenal can give Bruno Guimaraes perfect sweetener if £70million transfer goes through
Sports.content:
Arsenal can give Bruno Guimaraes perfect sweetener if £70million transfer goes through

Arsenal are stepping up their efforts to sign Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is pressing to join Arsenal (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

Arsenal can hand Bruno Guimaraes his cherished squad number if they can get a deal for the Newcastle midfielder over the line. The Brazilian is a top target for the Gunners, with the midfielder eager to join the Premier League champions.

‌



Newcastle are aware of Arsenal's interest but do not want to sell, having let Sandro Tonali join Tottenham for £100million earlier this summer. However, a trend has emerged regarding wanted Newcastle players, with the club initially digging their heels before eventually sanctioning a move.

‌



The Gunners will hope that is the case as they prepare to make a £70m bid for the 28-year-old. Despite their admiration for Guimaraes, they are reportedly unwilling to go beyond that figure.

‌



If Arsenal do sign Guimaraes, they would presumably hand him the number 39 shirt he has routinely worn in club football. He wears that number for a very special reason: it was the number on the taxi his father drove in Brazil.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Guimaraes credits his dad's support and sacrifice for helping him realise his football dreams. He once said: "The number on my shirt tells a story more beautiful than words can express. I know that people think it's a strange number for a footballer.

‌



5 attackers Arsenal could still sign after Morgan Rogers transfer setback READ MORE :

"But for me, the 39 is special. It's magical. The number 39 has given me everything in life. It brought me here to Newcastle. It fed me, clothed me and funded the trips that allowed me to realise my dream of becoming a footballer.

"The number 039 was my father's taxi number in Rio de Janeiro. My father drove that yellow taxi day and night so that I could eat.

"Now, when he walks through the streets of Newcastle, on the other side of the world, people stop him and ask for photos. That yellow taxi kept my dream alive."

‌



View 3 Images Guimaraes has always worn number 39 for his clubs (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

Following the unveiling of Arsenal's squad numbers for the new season, the 39 shirt is currently vacant, having belonged to youngster Harrison Dudziak last season. Previously, it has been worn by Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin.

Guimaraes arrived at St James' Park in a £35m switch from Lyon in January 2022 as Amanda Staveley’s consortium opened the purse strings three months after completing their takeover.

‌



View 3 Images Eddie Howe doesn't want to lose Guimaraes (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Initially nursed into the team by head coach Eddie Howe, he quickly established himself as a fans' favourite and, having been appointed captain, led the Magpies to their first major domestic trophy for 70 years in the 2024-25 Carabao Cup final.

Should he depart, he would leave a sizeable hole in a team already depleted by the departures of Tonali and Anthony Gordon, who has joined Barcelona.

Sports.title: World Cup star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after double police stop
Sports.content:
World Cup star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after double police stop

The Australian international made three appearances for the Socceroos at this summer's tournament.

View 2 Images Cristian Volpato was reportedly stopped twice by police for speeding. (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Australia international Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped by police twice in the same night in Sydney. The midfielder represented the Socceroos at this summer's World Cup in North America.

‌



NSW police report that Volpato was stopped for the first time at around 11pm local time for travelling between 86-94km/h in a 60km/h zone. He took a roadside breathalyser, which was negative.

‌



Just a couple of hours later, at around 1am, the 22-year-old in a BMW Coupe was said to have been stopped again after allegedly travelling at 109 km/h on the 60/km/h limited Anzac Bridge. This time, a roadside drug test allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine, with a second sample taken for further analysis.

‌



Argentina president goes on rant as calls for country to be banned from World Cup grow READ MORE :

Man Utd may have to scrap strict Arsenal transfer rule after latest Marcus Rashford blow READ MORE :

Volpato was handed a speeding fine and is reported to have had his international driver's licence suspended for six months, meaning that he is not permitted to drive in New South Wales. He has not been charged with a criminal offence, and the police have confirmed they will continue their enquiries.

The midfielder played three times for Australia during their World Cup campaign. After being an unused substitute for the opening game against Turkey, he featured in the other two group games against the USA and Paraguay, as well as the round of 32 penalty shootout loss vs Egypt.

View 2 Images Cristian Volpato has reportedly tested positive for cocaine.

‌



Volpato switched allegiances to Australia back in May, having represented Italy at youth level. His only international appearance for the nation before the World Cup came in a warm-up match against Switzerland in June.

In a statement, relayed by Australian outlet ABC, Australia football said it "was aware of the allegations involving one of our players."

Sports.title: Argentina president goes on rant as calls for country to be banned from World Cup grow
Sports.content:
Argentina president goes on rant as calls for country to be banned from World Cup grow

The fallout from the World Cup final continues, with Argentina's president Javier Milei busy posting on social media amid a backlash against his country after defeat by Spain

View 3 Images Javier Milei has been active on social media since the World Cup final (Image: Tomas Cuesta/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Argentina president Javier Milei has suggested that others are jealous of his country after a petition calling for them to be banned from future World Cups attracted over 23 million signatures.

‌



Argentina have been on the receiving end of a barrage of criticism following the shameful scenes after the final whistle in New Jersey. Spain overcame Lionel Messi and Co in extra time thanks to Ferran Torres' strike, but their victory was overshadowed by what followed.

‌



Midfielder Leandro Paredes kicked and punched as he shoved Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Gavi, while Nahuel Molina appeared to have instigated the altercation by throwing a punch at Rodri. FIFA are investigating the ugly scenes, which could prompt suspensions and fines.

‌



Argentina have been widely criticised for their behaviour, which came at the end of a match in which they mustered just two shots, committed regular fouls and had Enzo Fernandez sent off. An online petition calling for them to be banned from all future World Cups has now racked up 23,316,108 signatures from around 170 countries.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Argentina FA intervene as World Cup final conspiracy theories emerge after Spain win READ MORE :

Furious Argentina fans launch petition to replay 'corrupt' Spain World Cup final READ MORE :

But the backlash has only served to create a siege mentality in the South American country, with a rival petition launched arguing the match should be replayed due to a "corrupt" referee.

‌



Now right-wing leader Milei has amplified the feeling of injustice against his country through some posts on Instagram. The 55-year-old has shared a succession of posts which appear to defend the team.

"Do you have enemies? It means you once defended something. We defend Argentina," one reads. Another says: "The problem with Argentina is that we are conspicuous, we don't go unnoticed, people are jealous of us, and we are good at almost everything."

Milei also shared an AI image of him ripping open his suit to reveal an Argentina shirt with the caption "Long live Argentina, damn it!"

‌



View 3 Images Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the post-match fighting (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The nationalist rhetoric follows the semi-final win over England, which sparked more controversy after Argentina's players were shown celebrating with a banner which read "Las Malvinas son Argentinas", which translates as "The Falklands are Argentine".

The feeling has been echoed by many of Lionel Scaloni's squad, including arch villain Paredes, who refused to apologise for his behaviour after the final. "Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always. Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves," he wrote.

‌



"But with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again! Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team.

View 3 Images Argentina celebrated with this banner after defeating England (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

"To this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

‌



Paredes managed to avoid a red card for his actions, but along with team-mates Molina and Thiago Almada and assistant coach Roberto Ayala, could face disciplinary proceedings from FIFA.

World football's governing body has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess what happened after the final whistle at MetLife stadium. Those involved are facing suspensions, while the Argentine Football Association (AFA) can expect a hefty fine for failing to control players and staff.

Sports.content:
Man Utd may have to scrap strict Arsenal transfer rule after latest Marcus Rashford blow

Marcus Rashford still finds himself in transfer limbo ahead of the 2026/27 season after his dream move to Barcelona evaporated and with Manchester United's stance causing an issue

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford's future remains unresolved (Image: Richard Sellers/Allstar, Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford is currently away on holiday, where he is supposed to be relaxing and recuperating after a long season ended in disappointment with England at the World Cup. But he may be finding it hard to enjoy himself given his current situation.

‌



Rashford had a fantastic 2025/26 season. It hardly could have gone better, with 14 goals and 14 assists coming in 49 games during a dream loan spell with Barcelona. He ended the campaign by being named in Thomas Tuchel's squad for the World Cup.

‌



Months later and the Three Lions had to settle for third place and his preferred destination in club football failed to materialise. Rather than trigger a £26million option to sign him permanently, Barcelona opted to splash out £69m on Anthony Gordon before reinforcing their stance in a further blow to United by spending £18.7m on Karim Adeyemi.

‌



Any chance of Rashford joining Barca is surely gone and, at present, the most likely outcome is that he will return to United - the club he thought he'd said goodbye to for good. Rashford still has two years on his contract with his boyhood club, who hold the key to resolving his frustrating situation.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd can get £90million boost from six summer sales headlined by Marcus Rashford READ MORE :

Man Utd may have to change plans for two players after Marcus Rashford return READ MORE :

United want to cash in their chips and believed his impressive season with Barca would make doing so straightforward. But the Catalan side's attempt to negotiate another loan deal, rather than paying the agreed £26m clause, angered United executives and ultimately burned that bridge.

‌



The other major issue is Rashford's wages. He is being paid £325,000 per week by United, having signed a bumper five-year deal in July 2023. Those terms have effectively hamstrung Rashford, making him unattainable for other clubs.

The 28-year-old was willing to take a significant pay cut to join Barcelona, but things didn't work out. Now, if he is to escape United this summer, he needs the club to play ball.

View 2 Images Barcelona opted not to sign Marcus Rashford on a permanent deal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The only teams who realistically have the financial power to sign Rashford are in the Premier League. The i reports that Tottenham, Chelsea and Arsenal have been keeping an eye on him, yet United are currently unwilling to do business with a rival in the same league.

While his success with Barcelona was viewed positively last season, the thought of their academy graduate tearing it up in the Premier League is proving to be a powerful deterrent towards his sale.

United have strengthened their midfield this summer through the signings of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, with the sale of Rasmus Hojlund and the departures of Casemiro and Jadon Sancho helping free up funds. But Rashford remains the biggest piece of the jigsaw yet to be found a home.

‌



Michael Carrick has a good relationship with Rashford, who is understood to harbour no ill feelings towards the club now Ruben Amorim is long gone. Currently, he is set to join up with the United squad for the Irish training camp in early August.

If that is to change, then Rashford will need a huge change of heart from United's top brass.

‌



Following his impressive displays, Gabriel also spent time training alongside Michael Carrick's first-team squad last season. Premier League regulations prevented the forward from making his league debut, as academy players must have turned 15 before the end of August to feature in that particular season.

‌



Gabriel is now eligible for first-team action and could make his debut in the club's pre-season friendly against Rosenborg on Friday. The U18 Premier League Player of the Season missed United's recent 1-0 loss to Wrexham but was spotted in training earlier this week.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

With Gabriel possibly on the verge of another step forward in his fledgling career, United star Mbeumo has already offered his thoughts on where the prolific academy sensation could best slot into the side. "He's actually kind of a winger, he's a dribbler and even in front of the box, I still think he's good, honestly," Mbeumo told Zack En Roue Libre in March.

‌



"He's strong, the little guy is strong. Yeah, he's strong, he's really something, frankly... I think he's 15.

"You feel that he's bound to be a little kid but he trains quite a bit with us and actually you see, you can feel that the little guy has something special."

Gabriel is expected to travel with the United squad for their upcoming fixture against Rosenborg and has shown his determination to feature following the recent defeat to Wrexham. He posted on Instagram: "The longer you wait for something the more you appreciate it when you get it because anything worth having is worth waiting for."

‌



View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo spoke positively about Gabriel (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

The England U17 international is likely to receive some playing time during pre-season as he aims to build on his swift progression through United's academy system. He has yet to make his United U21s debut but now has a chance to prove himself at senior level, although manager Michael Carrick has previously urged caution.

Speaking about Gabriel's development last season, Carrick said: "He's doing really well, JJ. We've got some really good young players in the academy and we try and get the younger players up [with the first team] as much as we can.

‌



"We're always trying to give that exposure to the players to come and train and feel it."

View 3 Images Gabriel has been involved in pre-season training (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

The United manager added: "JJ is a big talent, it's pretty obvious to know that and he's had a really good season for the U18s. We obviously think an awful lot of him, but patience is important in managing everything that comes with that and working with him in development as we do with all the different younger players and picking the right moment to step up.

Article continues below

"What he's done when he's trained, he's done well, as you'd expect, and it's good to have the younger players come up with us."

Sports.title: Liverpool's dream squad for 2026/27 season as Rayan signs and £111m double deal sealed
Sports.content:
Liverpool's dream squad for 2026/27 season as Rayan signs and £111m double deal sealed

Liverpool are in the market for a new winger and there are more players who could arrive to create a dream squad for Andoni Iraola

View 4 Images Rayan could be Liverpool's marquee summer signing (Image: Getty)

Liverpool are in need of refining Andoni Iraola's squad for his maiden campaign. The blockbuster acquisition of Rayan and another £111million double-deal might achieve this.

‌



After failing to defend their Premier League crown, the Reds will return for the upcoming season with a new manager and their sights set on regaining the title from winners Arsenal. But, to do so, they'll need to reinforce.

‌



While Andy Robertson's, Mohamed Salah's and Ibrahima Konate's contracts all expired, Iraola has only welcomed two new recruits in Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz. Mirror Football takes a look at how the Reds can craft their dream squad, including spending big on a replacement for Salah.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Andoni Iraola now has something Arne Slot and Jurgen Klopp never did at Liverpool READ MORE :

Rayan arrives

There will be no Egyptian King at Anfield next season and with such an enormous presence absent, a suitable successor is needed. Rayan could be amongst the few wingers available who could fit in effortlessly.

Rio Ngumoha will probably be afforded substantial playing time by Iraola. However, he cannot shoulder the burden alone and if Bournemouth's Rayan is reunited with the manager who developed him last term, the possibilities are endless.

‌



View 4 Images Iraola is familiar with Rayan (Image: Getty)

In merely half a season, Iraola transformed Rayan from a raw Brazilian prospect into a forward who started for his nation at the World Cup aged just 19. Insufficient attention is being paid to what an extraordinary achievement this represented.

Liverpool securing him could prove challenging, as the Cherries have no incentive to release him and his £130m release clause becomes active in January. Yet Iraola understands the player and might compel their hand should Rayan grow restless.

‌



He would likely command upwards of £100m. Nevertheless, if Liverpool are forthright with their pursuit and the player desires the switch, would Bournemouth risk fielding a discontented star for an entire campaign?

Five first-team stars sold

To fund such a transfer and streamline the squad overall, there are four players Liverpool ought to attempt selling this summer. First and foremost, Federico Chiesa can depart.

While he represented a bargain when he joined from Juventus and remains a popular figure, should Rayan arrive, the Italian would see his game time curtailed even further. Ngumoha, Cody Gakpo and Munoz will all demand minutes.

‌



View 4 Images Chiesa, Elliott and Endo can all leave (Image: Getty)

In midfield, Curtis Jones' departure appears unavoidable as he's slipped down the pecking order and his 'pure profit' status under Profit and Sustainability Rules means he could prove pivotal in funding other transactions. Elsewhere, both Wataru Endo and Harvey Elliott are free to find themselves new clubs.

Elliott's departure would carry the same advantages as Jones' sale, whilst Endo, currently sidelined through injury, will be deemed surplus to requirements once he returns to fitness. To round off the exits, Kostas Tsimikas can also make a move after spending last season on loan with Roma. His contract expires in 2027 and he's just turned 30.

‌



Double deal sealed

With three midfielders sold, there would have to be at least one replacement signed and whilst it is very speculative, Liverpool could raid Borussia Dortmund for two of their brightest sparks.

Felix Nmecha was impressive for Germany at the World Cup and is a tall, physically imposing No. 8. He would bring something very different to Liverpool's midfield, which is, admittedly, brimming with talent already.

View 4 Images Nmecha and Svensson could be brilliant additions (Image: Getty)

‌



Although Nmecha is not a necessity, he could partner Ryan Gravenberch in midfield for more physically aggressive matches and Alexis Mac Allister's future in red is not streamlined. If Liverpool do make a move for Nmecha, valued at an estimated £86m, then they could swoop for Dortmund's left-back Daniel Svensson too.

Svensson is incredibly versatile, able to bomb forward as a wingback, defend deeper or even push into midfield. At £25m, a price reported in Germany, he would provide depth to Iraola's defensive options and give Milos Kerkez food for thought whilst replacing Tsimikas.

Full squad list

Goalkeepers: Alisson Becker, Giorgi Mamardashvili, Freddie Woodman.

‌



Defenders: Joe Gomez, Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Jeremie Frimpong.

Midfielders: Florian Wirtz, Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch, Trey Nyoni, Stefan Bajcetic.

Forwards: Alexander Isak, Rayan, Cody Gakpo, Hugo Ekitike, Rio Ngumoha.

Article continues below

Sold: Wataru Endo, Curtis Jones, Harvey Elliott, Federico Chiesa, Kostas Tsimikas.

Signed: Rayan, Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz, Felix Nmecha, Daniel Svensson.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta axes three Arsenal stars ahead of new season as squad revamp gathers pace
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta axes three Arsenal stars ahead of new season as squad revamp gathers pace

Mikel Arteta has given three Arsenal players the green light to leave the Emirates Stadium this summer

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is leading a squad revamp this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Three Arsenal players have already been axed by Mikel Arteta as the Spaniard continues his major squad overhaul this summer. The Gunners boss went into this transfer window knowing he had to improve the quality of his squad in order to retain the Premier League title next season.

‌



The first step in achieving this is to offload players who are considered to fall short of the required standard, while the second is to bring in signings that address gaps in the squad.

‌



Jakub Kiwior was the first player shown the door by Arteta this summer. The Pole completed a permanent switch to Porto earlier this month for £14.6million plus add-ons, following a loan spell with the Portuguese club last season.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

This follows the arrival of Piero Hincapie as a direct upgrade at the start of the 2025/26 campaign. Hincapie quickly became a crowd favourite at the Emirates Stadium last term, thanks to his dependable and passionate displays at the back, which proved crucial to their title triumph and earned him his own £34.5m permanent deal at N5 last month.

He was the direct successor to Kiwior as a physically imposing defender comfortable at both centre-back and left-back — only of a higher quality. Kiwior was well aware his opportunities in north London would be restricted even before Hincapie's arrival last summer, and Arteta granted him the chance to seek a fresh challenge elsewhere.

‌



Former reserve shot-stopper Karl Hein has also turned his loan move to Werder Bremen into a permanent transfer this month. The 24-year-old made his first-team debut in the EFL Cup third round clash against Brighton back in November 2022.

View 3 Images Jakub Kiwior was one of the first to leave Arsenal this summer (Image: Diogo Cardoso, Getty Images)

But that proved to be his only outing for the Gunners as he failed to establish himself in the first-team. Hein, who has been Estonia's number one at international level since 2020, was sent out on loan to Reading, Real Valladolid and Werder Bremen, with his spell in Germany coming last term.

‌



His permanent move to Bremen was confirmed in May, demonstrating he was also deemed surplus to requirements, with the move getting the green light from Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta. In his place, Arsenal boast several deputies to David Raya, including 20-year-old Tommy Setford, Kepa Arrizabalaga and the recently-signed Illan Meslier, who arrived on a free transfer from Leeds United earlier this month after putting pen to paper on a two-year contract.

Perhaps the most notable exit this summer has been Leandro Trossard's £17m move to Besiktas, confirmed last week. The Belgian was key in Arsenal clinching the title during the latter stages of last season, though his departure wasn't necessarily unexpected.

Aged 31 and with just 12 months remaining on his Arsenal contract, it was, in Arteta's view, the ideal moment to cash in on Trossard while creating the chance to enhance the left-wing role with fresh talent. Christos Tzolis has been recruited as Trossard's successor for a sum of £34m, taking Arsenal's summer spending to £68.5m.

‌



The Greek winger, 24, was brought in to deliver vital cover on the left side. Tzolis, who spent three seasons at Norwich City between 2021 and 2024, enjoyed an outstanding spell for Club Brugge last term, having registered 51 goal involvements across 52 matches.

View 3 Images Leandro Trossard has signed for Besiktas (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

Such deals have set things in motion in N5. While they may not prove as headline-grabbing as some of their competitors splashing over £100m on marquee players, they showcase astute business from both Arteta and Berta.

Article continues below

However, there is still considerable work to be done, with further exits anticipated as part of Arsenal's summer overhaul. Other players who could receive the green light to seek new pastures include Christian Norgaard, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and potentially Ethan Nwaneri.

More signings are also likely, with some £180m of the £250m budget Arteta was allocated this summer yet to be used. A world-class forward, a central midfielder and a defender are expected to arrive before the window closes on September 1.

Sports.title: Chelsea agree deal with Palace for Lacroix
Sports.content:
Chelsea have agreed a deal with Crystal Palace to sign Maxence Lacroix.

The 26-year-old defender has given permission to finalise the transfer. Palace were seeking around £55m in negotiations given the fee Tottenham paid for Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton.

Sky Sports News understands Chelsea have given Palace the chance to discuss signing one of their defenders available for transfer during talks.

There has been interest from other clubs in Axel Disasi, Trevoh Chalobah and Benoit Badiashile.

Palace and Chelsea have a good relationship and they have done deals for players such as Chalobah and Ben Chilwell in the past.

The Eagles have been concentrating on Augsburg centre-back Chrislain Matsima. However, Sky Sports News understands they are now prepared to walk away from the deal, having become frustrated with the speed of negotiations.

Palace have been interested in several centre-backs since the January window when Marc Guehi was sold to Manchester City.

Among those have been Toulouse's Charlie Cresswell, Lyon's Ruben Kluivert and Trabzonspor's Chibuke Nwaiwu, who is also of interest to Fulham.

Sky Sports' Adam Bate:

Chelsea have not paid a transfer fee for a player aged 26 or over since the summer of 2022 with the ill-fated acquisitions of Raheem Sterling and Kalidou Koulibaly. But Crystal Palace's Maxence Lacroix is a player worth relaxing the policy for.

Far from a veteran, Lacroix, 26, is entering his prime after two strong seasons with Palace. Beyond Selhurst Park, perhaps the Frenchman has gone a little under the radar. But, particularly since Marc Guehi's exit, there is growing awareness of his key role.

Image: Maxence Lacroix's top speed for Crystal Palace in the Premier League

Oliver Glasner, who worked with him in both Germany and England, rather summed it up with his own verdict on the player recently. "There is Maxence Lacroix, who came from Wolfsburg, and many asked, 'Why did you sign this player?' I think he stepped up."

Few defenders boast his skillset. Lacroix ranks among the top five fastest centre-backs in the Premier League since his arrival from Wolfsburg in 2024. That recovery speed helps make him one of the most formidable one-on-one defenders in the competition.

The numbers back that up to. In one-on-one situations, nobody is better than Lacroix at winning the ball back. He is the only player in the Premier League to have faced 50 or more such situations in the past two seasons and won the ball more often than not.

Image: Maxence Lacroix's one-on-one defending for Crystal Palace in the Premier League

At 6'4" tall, Lacroix is a robust physical presence who has adapted easily to the demands of the Premier League. He has all the stats to support that, ranking third for clearances and seventh for aerial duels won. But he can do more than defend his box.

Sports.title: Doyle: Masquerade Ball can clinch historic King George win
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle reveals her thoughts on the King George at Ascot on Saturday and runs the rule over the best of the other weekend action at Ascot and York.

Momentous success on cards for Japan

Japan has held a special place in my heart since riding in Tokyo for three winters, so I'll be rooting for their superstar MASQUERADE BALL in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes (3.35) at Ascot on Saturday.

Takahisa Tezuka's colt has unfinished business with the mighty Calandagan after losing out right on the line in the Japan Cup back in November. Since then, he has finished a gallant second to Hong Kong's Romantic Warrior in the QEII Cup while the French ace has added the Sheema Classic and the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud to his amazing CV.

Whatever happens, it's going to be a thriller with Aidan O'Brien's Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini getting a lot of weight from the pair but I have a feeling that everything is in place for Masquerade Ball to give the Japanese one of their most momentous successes ever. A year younger than Calandagan and still capable of better, he can take revenge as long as the uphill finish doesn't catch him out.

Moonrise can build on Royal Ascot form

MOONRISE can enhance her reputation in the big two-year-old fillies' race at Ascot, the Group 3 Princess Margaret Japan Cup Stakes (1.45).

Andrew Balding's daughter of Churchill took a step up in grade in her stride when finishing a close third in the Windsor Castle Stakes at the Royal Meeting and the combination of a good attitude and track form can make her hard to beat.

Richard Hannon's Dark Issue was fourth in the Group 3 Albany Stakes at this track last month - form that has since been franked by the runner-up, Sun Goddess, taking a Group 2 in Ireland for Aidan O'Brien - but Oisin Murphy's filly offers better value.

Moore booking looks significant in Valiant

There is no denying that Owen Burrows' filly Touleen was unlucky in the Coronation Stakes last time when she split two Guineas winners, despite enduring such a difficult passage.

She'll be a worthy favourite for the Group 3 Longines Valiant Stakes (2.20) under William Buick, but I prefer to side with Jane Chapple-Hyam's KON TIKI with Ryan Moore another significant booking.

Open to improvement, she is more than capable of winning at this level and shouldn't find this quite as demanding at the Group 2 Duke Of Cambridge when she chased home Blue Bolt for the second time this year.

Unbeaten Zain to take ultra-tough International

My husband Tom (Marquand) holds a favourite's chance in the Moet And Chandon International Handicap (2.55) at Ascot on the unbeaten EXTREMELY ZAIN, who has the potential to ply his trade in Pattern races later in the year.

Image: Extremely Zain returns to action on Saturday

He didn't enjoy the best of runs in a hot handicap at York last time but still found a way through to post an impressive success under Cieren Fallon and has the scope to defy an 8lb rise from what looks a decent draw.

This is ultra-tough though so keep an eye on Jack Channon's Mezcala, the Buckingham Palace winner for Tom who also has more to offer despite reappearing off a stiffer mark of 98.

Champion the one to beat in York feature

I am disappointed to see the Sky Bet York Stakes (2.35) at York attract only five runners, but it is a quality field, headed by the magnificent globetrotter ROYAL CHAMPION.

Karl Burke's eight-year-old has been given a well-deserved break since winning the valuable Neom Turf Cup in Saudi Arabia and finishing fourth behind Romantic Warrior and Masquerade Ball in Hong Kong.

Tough, resilient, and capable of finding his best form fresh, Royal Champion has less to prove than Dante winner Item, who may have had ground excuses in the Epsom Derby but now needs to take a big step forward to win this Group 2.

Ryan sprinter out to build on strong Chester run

The Sky Bet Dash Handicap (2.00) at York has a wide-open feel so I'm opting for value in Kevin Ryan's locally trained WE NEVER STOP, who looks set to go off a big price in the 6f feature.

Having his second start following wind surgery, he can build on an encouraging close second at Chester last month for a trainer who excels on The Knavesmire.

I expected Addison Grey to win after chasing home the subsequent Wokingham Winner Double Rush at Newmarket, but Clive Cox's grey hasn't capitalised in two runs since. Still, an unchanged mark of 94 should see him firmly in the mix once again.

Stepping up my rehab after positive news

Since getting the go-ahead last week to begin weight bearing on my broken left leg, I have been upping my rehabilitation routine at Oaksey House in Lambourn.

I'm working out there five days a week under the supervision of an excellent team, putting in some strong sessions in the gym, on the bike and in the hydro pool with the aim of achieving more movement.

It's a long road back from the injury I sustained in a fall at Bath in May, but it feels good to finally be more active.

Sports.title: DeChambeau reveals Open penalty frustration
Sports.content:
Bryson DeChambeau has spoken for the first time about the controversial two-shot penalty he believes cost him a shot at winning The Open.

DeChambeau was remarkably penalised in his second round after officials reviewed footage and ruled he had improved the area of his backswing by flattening some long grass on Royal Birkdale's fifth hole.

The penalty turned his bogey into a triple-bogey seven, which moved him from outright second to fifth in the standings at the midway point.

DeChambeau threatened to withdraw from the tournament in protest but played on, making it through to the weekend to end a run of three consecutive missed cuts in majors and avoid the 'Bryson Slam' of missing all four in a season.

But despite recovering with rounds of 69 and 72 he was left wondering what might have been after finishing six shots behind winner Ryan Fox.

"I made the cut," DeChambeau told a LIV Golf UK press conference.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bryson DeChambeau was given a two-shot penalty after inadvertently improving his lie in thick rough on the fifth hole at The Open.

"It was a good fight. I wish I'd have given it more on Saturday and Sunday, it felt like I could have.

"Besides the fifth, being three over on it, and the 11th, that's six shots. That's tied for the lead right there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scottie Scheffler defended Ryder Cup teammate Bryson DeChambeau after he was given a 2 shot penalty during the second round of the Open.

"Two holes and I'm right there for the Claret Jug."

World No 1 Scheffler defended DeChambeau over the rules controversy, insisting his fellow American is "not a cheater", while Rory McIlroy described the incident as "performative".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy spoke to the media after his third round of The Open and said he was not impressed with Bryson DeChambeau's actions that led to his two-stroke penalty after the second round.

"I won't pretend to be up here and defend Bryson," McIlroy said on Saturday. "I'm not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it's performative. I think a lot of it's for attention.

"To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn't feel like it was a great look."

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Silver Dominion faces Alfred Wallace at Ascot
Sports.content:
It's Silver Dominion versus Alfred Wallace as King George weekend gets under way at Ascot - live on Sky Sports Racing.

2.55 Ascot - Classy pair Silver Dominion and Alfred Wallace reoppose in feature

The Listed Flexjet Pat Eddery Stakes looks a belter with Silver Dominion and Alfred Wallace reopposing at Ascot.

Silver Dominion finished just ahead of Alfred Wallace when they were fourth and fifth in the Group Two July Stakes at Newmarket just 13 days ago and should have obvious claims in these calmer waters. Hector Crouch returns for the ride aboard the Oliver Cole-trained colt, with the Whatcombe-based trainer reporting his charge to be in fine form. Connections feel this is a good opportunity for their progressive prodigy.

Alfred Wallace has plenty of experience and could prove hard to peg back if given a soft lead under champion jockey Oisin Murphy, who knows favourite Silver Dominion well - having ridden him the last day. Trainer Ed Walker has a 24 per cent strike-rate when teaming up with Murphy throughout their careers - a stat which could see the Kingsdown Stables representative attract market support.

Gymbaazy made a winning start to his career when outpointing the odds-on favourite at Sandown last month and, given his inexperience in the finish, he should improve with racing. Trainer Owen Burrows is operating at a 38 per cent strike-rate, having tasted success with three of his last eight runners.

Others to consider include Treasurer and the hat-trick-seeking Kach Above.

4.05 Ascot - Al Azd and French Duke headline strong contest

A terrific edition of the Sodexo Live! Handicap where French Duke and Al Azd will be popular in the market.

Roger Varian's Al Azd has improved with each start since tackling handicap company and found only Enceladus too good when an excellent second at the Royal meeting. This trip and track seem to suit, and he must be feared despite an 8lb rise in the ratings.

Top-weight French Duke showed he retains plenty of ability when winning at Meydan in January but will need to step up on his recent form. The Wathnan Racing five-year-old is off level weights with Al Azd but has struggled on his three outings over course and distance - although all were in ultra-competitive Royal Ascot fields.

The Charlie Appleby-trained Study Of Words rates the best of the rest as he hopes to bounce back from a short-price reversal at Doncaster.

2.20 Ascot - Exciting duo Ash Tree and Blue Flight lock horns

The opening Sports4Causes October Club EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes sees a range of potentially-useful fillies clash over six furlongs.

Blue Flight, who was entered in the Princess Margaret on Saturday, showed a smart change of gear when landing a Yarmouth maiden on her first start and looks a promising type. Danny Muscutt retains the ride on the Blue Point filly, who flies the flag for the Cheveley Park operation.

Ash Tree was given a positive mention by her trainer in a recent interview and made a pleasing debut when scoring at Nottingham. Showing signs of greenness that day, she ought to improve for the run and be in the mix for Jane Chapple-Hyam.

Sorrengail, related to Space Blues, finished an eye-catching fourth with Speed Of Sound in third on debut at Newmarket and both have solid claims in a deep contest.

Others

Also at Ascot, the Class Three John Guest Racing Brown Jack Handicap (3.30pm) sees Fireblade and Synergism face off, with the latter not outside the first three in his last three starts for Sir Mark Prescott. Kircher is also worthy of a mention after chasing home Align The Stars in the Northumberland Plate, though he has been raised 2lb for that effort.

The card in Berkshire closes with the Sodexo Live! Fillies' Handicap (5.12pm), headlined by Desert Treasure and Paradise Walk.

Elsewhere, Colegram makes her handicap debut for the Dan Skelton team in Uttoxeter's Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle (3.50pm) but will have to contend with the challenge posed by Rock Hurley. Later on the card, the Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle (4.25pm) is the stage for Divilabother's hat-trick bid.

Chepstow plays host to a seven-race Flat card, with Kodi Fire topping seven runners in the feature LSL Racing Horse Sales Handicap (7.01pm).

Sports.title: Why Newcastle are looking to emulate German giants on recruitment
Sports.content:
When the Saudi PIF takeover of Newcastle was completed in late 2021 the new ownership set about adding age and experience to their newly acquired investment.

By the end of their first January transfer window Kieran Trippier, Chris Wood and Dan Burn, all in their late 20s and early 30s with more than 1,200 professional appearances between them, had done just that.

Younger, highly-rated players in Bruno Guimaraes from Lyon, Real Sociedad's Alexander Isak and Italy midfielder Sandro Tonali Everton winger Anthony Gordon followed over the next 18 months as Newcastle's philosophy began to cement to blend quality, experience and potential to gatecrash the Premier League's big boys.

But while the Toon Army have seen two Champions League campaigns come and go and have won their first silverware in generations, an elusive title race has never materialised.

Instead, after a nightmare summer in 2025, Eddie Howe's side were forced to swallow the pill of finishing five points off newly-promoted arch-rivals Sunderland last season - and closer to the relegation zone than a Champions League qualifying spot.

The head coach demanded this transfer window was different, and it certainly has been. Under a new recruitment team led by Ross Wilson, Newcastle have been among the busiest players with a month to go before the start of the season and have already completed three signings and are close on a fourth in Monaco's Aladji Bamba.

That is not the only way things have changed. The incoming quartet have played just 261 professional games between them and Lewis Miley aside, represent the four youngest senior players currently in Howe's squad for this season.

It is an intentional change.

Where the St James' Park hierarchy have looked for inspiration on how best to utilise the club's situation, given PSR constraints and the lure of Premier League rivals, they have found Borussia Dortmund a source of inspiration, after the German side's work on the likes of Jude Bellingham, Jadon Sancho and Erling Haaland in recent years.
