Sports.title: Argentina star who PUNCHED Spain rival in shameful World Cup final antics hints at quitting international football after 'painful' defeat - but finally admits new world champions 'were the better team'
Sports.content:
Argentina's chief aggressor from the World Cup final, Leandro Paredes, is considering quitting international football.

The midfielder, who grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the neck and pushed over Gavi after full time, says the 'pain' of losing will remain with him for a long time.

Paredes was heavily scrutinised for his outburst, during which he appeared to throw punches, and he was fortunate not to be sent off towards the end of normal time for a foul.

It comes as Argentina seem to be headed for a rebuild. Manager Lionel Scaloni was in tears as he hinted at his exit, while Nicolas Otamendi has already announced his retirement. Whether Lionel Messi continues remains to be seen – he is now 39.

Paredes, 32, told ESPN: 'For many, it will be the time to decide if to continue. It was a great journey. Maintaining that level – getting the group to continue to function as it has - will be very difficult, and there are many factors to consider.

'Decisions must be taken calmly. I don't know yet if I'm ready to continue. It's a process that takes time to assimilate and mature.

Argentina's chief aggressor from the World Cup final, Leandro Paredes, could quit international football

The midfielder, who lashed out at Spain's stars at full time, says the 'pain' of defeat will linger

'It will take time to digest what we've been through. The pain of losing the World Cup final will stay with us for a long time, because we came so close once again. I think we played in a World Cup where people saw themselves in us, and that's very rewarding. In that sense, I'm happy.'

FIFA have launched an investigation into the behaviour of the Argentina squad, who turned their backs on Spain during the trophy celebration after losing 1-0 to a Ferran Torres goal.

Spain star Gavi has since insisted that Paredes should not be suspended, but the Argentine was panned by BBC Sport's pundits.

Micah Richards said: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time. Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest.

'Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Fellow BBC pundit Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney also gave his views and said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina's players could also face further disciplinary action after FIFA opened an investigation following their semi-final win over England when several of them lifted a controversial banner touting their country’s claim to the Falkland Islands, which read: 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas'.

Argentina star Nicolas Otamendi has retired - after losing the World Cup final and clashing with Rodri

At least Paredes has put the final behind him in some way - he was back playing for Boca Juniors in the Copa Sudamericana this week.

Meanwhile, Otamendi has already walked away from international football.

The former Manchester City star and 2022 World Cup winner has said he is retiring from Argentina with his 'head held high' and with 'peace of mind'.

That's despite the 38-year-old's final act on the global stage being an angry row with Rodri, in which he branded the Spain captain an 'idiot' and accused the victors of whining too much.

The centre-back came on as a substitute on Sunday and was highly involved in Argentina's rearguard action. Spain's first goal by Nico Williams was ruled out because of the controversial call that Mikel Merino had fouled Otamendi.

He steps away after 139 caps – the fifth-most ever for Argentina – and eight goals. Having made his debut for them in 2009, he also went on to lift two Copa Americas.

Otamendi wrote on Instagram: 'Today I have to write the most difficult words of my entire career.

'From a very young age, I dreamed of wearing the Argentine national team jersey; it was the greatest privilege football has given me. I defended it with my soul, with pride, and with the responsibility of knowing what it means to millions of Argentinians.

Otamendi won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina and earned 139 caps for them, the fifth-most in the team's history

'Fate decreed that my last match would be a World Cup final. It wasn't the result we wanted, but I leave with my head held high, knowing that this group tried until the very last second.

'I say goodbye with the peace of mind of having given everything. I never held back an ounce of effort, I never stopped believing, and I never stopped feeling this jersey as the greatest honor of my life.

'Thank you to the Argentine fans. Thank you for your unconditional love, for every flag, for every song, for being with us in the good times and, above all, in the most difficult. You made us feel, every time the anthem played, that we weren't just eleven players, but millions defending the same dream.

'Thank you to my family. They were my refuge in every fall and my strength in every challenge. They endured the distances, the absences, the tears, and the frustrations. I never walked this path alone; we took every step together.

'And to those who still wear this jersey today, I want to say something from the bottom of my heart: never stop believing. There will be blows that seem impossible to overcome, but this jersey always rewards those who defend it with humility, sacrifice, and love. Hold your heads high, keep fighting, and don't let a defeat steal your hope. I am convinced that the next chapter of our story will be yours.

'Today I say goodbye to the Argentine national team, but with immense pride for having represented my country. Because titles remain in history, but the love for these colors lasts a lifetime.

'Thank you, Argentina. Thank you for letting me fulfil the dream of being a world champion and wearing the most beautiful jersey in the world.'

Otamendi has said he is walking away with his 'head held high' and with 'peace of mind'

Otamendi got embroiled in a post-match row with Rodri, saying: 'Start talking less, idiot. You guys spent the whole week crying.

'You spent the whole week crying. You and [Aymeric] Laporte, both of you. That's not how it's done. You were crying to the referees all week, my friend.'

Earlier in the week, Laporte had told Spanish outlet Marca: 'I'm not worried at all about physical play as long as it's part of football.

'If the referee does his job, I have no problem with it. It's true that in recent matches we've seen things that have surprised us, situations that have been allowed to go unpunished.

'Especially with Argentina, which is a team that likes to leave little messages with its challenges.

'That shouldn't be allowed in football, particularly in tournaments of this magnitude, because it can unsettle you and make you lose your composure.

'It's the referee's job to keep those situations under control so the match doesn't get away from him.

'If one or two players are allowed to do whatever they want, the game will become chaotic. Since the beginning of the tournament, we've been a very fair team in that regard.

'We don't go around kicking opponents or making reckless fouls, and I think that's the approach we have to maintain in this match. But, of course, a lot will depend on the officiating.'

Sports.title: Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog reveals betting line opened just moments after US striker was sent off at the World Cup
Sports.content:
Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog reveals betting line opened just moments after US striker was sent off at the World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A gambling watchdog group has flagged the United States' Round-of-16 loss to Belgium as one of seven World Cup matches that may have drawn irregular betting activity during the tournament.

Specifically, the independent Group of Copenhagen cited a predictions market line titled 'Will Folarin Balogun play against Belgium?' as one potential issue, sources told The Athletic.

That line opened on July 2 shortly after Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. On July 5, after President Donald Trump urged FIFA to rescind Balogun's red card, the governing body opted instead to suspend his one-game ban until after the tournament, thereby allowing him to play in the loss to Belgium.

Curiously, the Group of Copenhagen's report specified that no other similar markets opened for the 14 other players who got a red card during the tournament, according to The Athletic. Now the group has requested an official explanation from FIFA on the Balogun case.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from both FIFA and Polymarket, neither of which have been accused of any misconduct in this case.

Operating under the Council of Europe's Macolin Convention of 2014, the Group of Copenhagen is an independent network that detects and prevents the manipulation of sports competitions around the world. For the 2026 World Cup, the organization reviewed all 104 matches from the tournament, which attracted more than $240 billion bets worldwide, according to the Group of Copenhagen.

A gambling watchdog has opened an investigation into Balogun's red card overhaul

Folarin Balogun (20) fouls Bosnia's Tarik Muharemovic (4), resulting in a red card

Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia

Although its full report has not yet been published, a summary of its conclusions has been shared by the Council of Europe.

The US loss to Belgium was among seven 'yellow notices' raised by the Group of Copenhagen, which has two higher levels of concern: orange and red.

'The Group of Copenhagen's notices can be explained by atypical behaviors such as changes in odds or hedging liquidities, there are many explanations that are not manipulations,' Christian Kalb, a gambling industry expert who previously worked with the Group of Copenhagen, told The Athletic.

'The major problem is when there may be a conflict of interest and potential inside information on those issues,' she continued. 'When we speak of prediction markets, we can detect some unusual behaviors but we must be very careful as they can be used for hedging markets.

The Norwegian FA is planning to complain to FIFA over the Folarin Balogun World Cup saga

Meanwhile, the Norwegian FA plans to launch a formal complaint to FIFA over Trump's interference in Balogun's red card ban.

Despite Trump's interventions, the US were thrashed 4-1 by Belgium, yet the 80-year-old has repeatedly boasted about his involvement, adding that FIFA President Gianni Infantino made a 'great decision.'

The antics of Trump and FIFA were widely condemned across the sport, and Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness now says she is planning to formally complain to the governing body's ethics committee.

'When you bend a rule like this, you're on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,' she said. 'It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.

'First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.

'If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behavior and the organization's behavior, and also the red line of what states' leaders should interfere with. And that happened.'

Defending his role in the saga, Infantino insisted it was an independent decision taken by FIFA's disciplinary committee.

He said: 'They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA's disciplinary code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

'Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.'

Sports.title: Why Arsenal paid £34m for Norwich flop Christos Tzolis: The problem insiders insist Greece star will solve, similarities with Leandro Trossard and what it means for Gunners' forward hunt
Sports.content:
Why Arsenal paid £34m for Norwich flop Christos Tzolis: The problem insiders insist Greece star will solve, similarities with Leandro Trossard and what it means for Gunners' forward hunt

Unlock more from Isaan Khan inside the Arsenal camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Rewind to September 2021. Norwich City’s record signing Christos Tzolis arrived at the Emirates to face an Arsenal team bottom of the Premier League table on zero points.

Five years later, after an ill-fated spell at the Canaries and a fast rise in the Belgian Pro League, Greek winger Tzolis now finds himself signing for the Premier League champions in a £34million deal from Club Bruges. It’s a remarkable turnaround for both parties.

The 24-year-old recorded an extraordinary 40 goal contributions (17 goals, 23 assists) in 36 league appearances last season, which landed him on Mikel Arteta’s radar.

It wasn’t an anomaly for Tzolis, either, having arrived in Belgium fresh off a loan spell with Bundesliga 2 side Fortuna Dusseldorf. There he mustered 34 goal contributions in 37 games. His performance in Greece’s 2-1 Nations League victory over England at Wembley in October 2024 also caught the eye.

With Leandro Trossard having joined Besiktas, Tzolis is the like-for-like replacement. The comparisons between the pair are interesting. They both played in the Belgian Pro League, are proficient in front of goal and are pacy, adaptable attackers.

The Greek forward is predominantly a winger like Trossard, but can also play as a No 10. Last summer, for example, Crystal Palace strongly considered Tzolis as a replacement for Eberechi Eze.

Christos Tzolis recorded an extraordinary 40 goal contributions (17 goals, 23 assists) in 36 league appearances last season for Club Bruges

The 24-year-old is predominantly a winger but can also play as a No 10

Hayk Milkon, Club Bruges' assistant manager until February, previously said: ‘He's able to fulfil different roles. Coming from the left side — giving him this space to start wide and then find the moments to get more inside — that's where he's at his strongest.

‘If he's assigned to play really wide to get these one-on-ones, he's able to do it. But he's always strongest the closer he is to the goal. Whenever he's more central, you can expect him at any moment to attack the space.’

Another similarity between Tzolis and Trossard is their availability. Trossard was only injured for four matches in three-and-a-half-years at Arsenal, those games coming in his final season in north London. Tzolis has a similar record at Club Bruges, missing just two matches due to injury across two seasons.

The new arrival is two-footed but likes to cut in from the left on to his right foot where he can provide fizzing passes or make inroads to goal. His shooting efficiency, paired with an unpredictability of whether he hugs the touchline or cuts in, can cause havoc.

Goals from their wingers is an area in which the Gunners are aiming to improve. Last season, among Arsenal’s wide attackers, none reached double figures in the Premier League. One man who will be looking over his shoulder is Gabriel Martinelli. The Brazilian scored just one league goal last term. Arsenal’s left-wing spot is up for grabs.

Tzolis will need time to adapt to a new league, though, and therein lies comparisons to another Arsenal forward: Viktor Gyokeres. The Swede started slowly before getting going in the second half of last season to round off the campaign with 21 goals across all competitions. Gyokeres had a failed spell in England with Brighton before moves to Coventry and Sporting Lisbon kickstarted his career.

There is some caution to be had around Tzolis’ output, of course. The Belgium Pro League is the eighth strongest league in the world, according to Opta's Power Rankings — one place below the Championship.

And what is also clear is that Tzolis has very big boots to fill. Affectionately dubbed ‘Mr Clutch’ by supporters for his habit of striking in crucial moments, Trossard leaves Arsenal as a cult hero who proved great value for his £27m move from Brighton in January 2023.

Tzolis has managed nine goals for Greece across his 34 appearances

He will be charged with filling the void left by Arsenal cult hero Leandro Trossard, who has joined Besiktas in Turkey

Across the 2025 calendar year, Trossard registered more goal contributions than any Arsenal player, with 13 goals and 12 assists. Mikel Merino followed with 13 goals and eight assists, while Declan Rice managed nine goals and 11 assists.

Trossard's late winner against West Ham in May, a pivotal moment in Arsenal becoming champions, underlines why he became such a trusted figure under Arteta. Such an impact will be hard to replicate at Premier League level for Tzolis.

The impending arrival of the Greek international, who has nine goals in 34 appearances for his country, doesn’t halt Arsenal’s plan to bring in more attacking reinforcements this summer. They retain an interest in Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez and Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola.

The challenge for Tzolis is proving his remarkable numbers in Belgium can translate to England. If he can do that, Arsenal may have found the long-term successor to one of Arteta’s most trusted attackers.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's bouts are fights in name only - their opponents are merely useful punchbags who'd be unlikely to get work as their sparring partners: JEFF POWELL MBE
Sports.content:
It will be possible to be at ringside to watch Tyson Fury box in Thailand this Friday evening and then attend Anthony Joshua’s fight in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night.

The Gypsy King will prove that by flying from Bangkok to Riyadh soon after his encounter with the veteran Mariusz Wach in time to see AJ take on somebody called Kristian Prenga.

It is safe to presume that precious few, if any, of their respective thousands of fans will join Fury on that journey or pitch up at either occasion. And not only because many of them will have sacrificed a year or two’s wages, perhaps their mortgages, maybe their marriages on England’s ill-fated World Cup expedition.

Even the rich boys on tour are likely to jib at forking out another small fortune to attend distant events which are fights in name only. Joshua’s flight booking gives the game away, as does the choice of venues. No capital cities this time. Fury goes through the motions in the notorious Thai beach resort of Pattaya. Joshua at Saudi Arabia’s Jeddah-on-sea.

Of course these are by way of preparation for them fighting each other in that forever awaited box-office boomer later this year. But to be honest these match-ups are not so much warm-ups as water-treaders. These opponents would be unlikely to get work as their sparring partners.

Describing Poland’s Mariusz Wach as a ring veteran is actually an understatement of his decline since he went into a world heavyweight title fight against Wladimir Klitschko as 27-0 unbeaten challenger. He not only lost that night in Germany 14 years ago but failed a drugs test which interrupted for two years his descent into today’s 39 wins, 13 defeats record.

Anthony Joshua is back in action on Saturday when he faces Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia

Tyson Fury is fighting Mariusz Wach in Bangkok on Friday as he prepares to secure a long-awaited bout with Joshua

The longer he drags on, as he approaches his 46th birthday, the more he becomes a useful punch-bag, given his masochistic capacity to absorb punches for several rounds. A painful service he has provided to a number of British heavyweights, Dillian Whyte, Frazer Clarke and Hughie Fury among them. This is so patently a mismatch that it is not being televised anywhere in the world, but being saved by Netflix to help promote Fury v Joshua when that finally comes around,

Two years ago Wach was flattened in as many rounds by our world heavyweight champion-in-waiting Moses Itauma. That mercifully swift ending made for more comfortable viewing than some of the pointless beatings he has taken down the years. Make it quick, Tyson.

Kristian Prenga is a virtually unknown entity outside his native Albania. He has passed almost equally unnoticed on undercards mostly around New York, New Jersey, Philadelphia and across the Canadian border since he emigrated to the US.

At least he is ten years younger than Wach and has 20 knock-out wins on his record against one points defeat. Not that you are likely to recognise any of the names on that dance card. Try Joey Dawejko, Aldo Callendar, Tim Chemelli, Willie Jake Jr, or the only man to beat him Giovanni Auriemma. Me neither. Most of them appear to have other jobs, such as barmen, bouncers or cab drivers.

Prenga, a pleasant enough feller, made the right noises at his London press conference: ‘A J and his team have made a mistake. They’ve overlooked my knock-out record. They’ve forgotten that he can no longer take a big punch like mine. Get ready for the world-wide shock which will change my life forever.’

He seems not to have noted that AJ is a former Olympic gold medallist and two-time world heavyweight champion. Nor that he is stepping into an altogether higher realm. Nor that Joshua is highly motivated emotionally by this being his first fight since his two close friends and team members were killed in a car crash in Africa which he was lucky to survive. ‘This is for them,’ he says. Get it done early, AJ. before he has a chance to land.

Fury is set to fly from Bangkok to Saudi Arabia to watch Joshua a day after his own fight

Then you can invite Fury to join you in the ring – ‘but don’t forget Tyson I’m the landlord for this one’ – so they can start the big sell.

November is the likely month for Fury v Joshua 1. Wembley the stadium of choice but only if Brent Council agree to lift their usual 11 pm curfew and permit it to be transmitted live to the American TV audience at somewhere between 2 am and 4 am London Sunday time.

So enormous will be the difference from this weekend that Fury is about to entertain no more than a thousand or so locals in a small, screened-off hall. He is donating the revenue from those tickets to good causes in Thailand, of which he has become fond as a training camp. It will be charity all-round. What with Wach and Prenga picking up probably the biggest purses of their lives for their roles as fall guys. But what if the inconceivable did happen?

Not only would the gigantic pay-days of Fury’s and Joshua’s last hurrah go down the drain but at least one or maybe both their careers would be terminated.

Don’t dare mention it.

*Fury v Wach this Friday night will be for private screening only.

*Joshua v Prenga will be televised live on DAZN pay-per-view this Saturday night

*Fury v Joshua is expected to be televised live to Netflix subscribers in the early hours one Sunday morning in November

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua refuses to talk about Tyson Fury clash ahead of comeback fight against Kristian Prenga - with bout versus the Gypsy King on the cards if both stars win this weekend
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua shut down talk of Tyson Fury and insisted there is 'no future' beyond Saturday night unless he first gets the job done against Kristian Prenga in Jeddah.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain showdown with Fury is edging ever closer, with both heavyweights taking interim bouts this weekend before an expected blockbuster collision later this year.

Fury boxes Mariusz Wach in Thailand on Friday before Joshua makes his return against the heavy-hitting Albanian less than 24 hours later.

But despite the frenzy surrounding what could finally become one of British boxing's biggest-ever fights, Joshua made it clear he has no interest in looking past the man standing across the ring from him.

'Look, respect my opponent here,' Joshua said when questions during Thursday's press conference turned towards Fury.

'We don't want to talk about Tyson Fury. Respectfully, I have done all the media that I can about what the future holds but you know our focus is him and his team.

Anthony Joshua (left) is refusing to entertain talk of a clash with Tyson Fury ahead of his comeback fight

'We have been working since January, working hard, keeping my head down, aligned all my stars and I am fully focused.'

Joshua acknowledged the excitement surrounding what could await him if he comes through unscathed, but stressed that those conversations count for nothing unless he delivers in Saudi Arabia.

'I understand there is a big picture. The goal is to conquer the universe, right? But first we must conquer earth. My target is here.'

It is a mindset forged by the toughest period of his life.

Saturday marks Joshua's first appearance since stopping Jake Paul in Miami last December, just days before tragedy struck when close friends Latif 'Latz' Ayodele and Sina Ghami were killed in a car accident in Nigeria.

The devastating loss forced Joshua away from boxing as he grieved, with serious doubts over whether he would ever fight again.

Instead, he eventually returned to training and rebuilt towards what could become the defining final chapter of his career.

Victory over Prenga is expected to pave the way for the fight fans have demanded for more than a decade, but Joshua insists he cannot afford to think beyond the immediate task.

Fury (pictured) and Joshua are expected to clash this year but must first both win this weekend

'When you speak to me about what may lay ahead or I sit down in an office with Eddie (Hearn) and he presents to me what may lay ahead, it is a great opportunity for me to understand where this checkpoint takes me and what it leads me on to,' Joshua said.

'The reality of the matter is there is no universe, there is no future unless I get past this checkpoint on Saturday night.'

Prenga arrives in Jeddah with 20 knockouts to his name, although the Albanian has never shared the ring with an opponent anywhere near Joshua's calibre.

For the 35-year-old, however, Saturday represents the opportunity he has spent a lifetime chasing.

'I work all my life for this, I waited all my life for this and I hope I am going to show the world on Saturday who I am,' Prenga said.

Sports.title: Shocking moment Bryson DeChambeau's wayward drive nearly hits a fuming Ian Poulter on the head
Sports.content:
Ian Poulter narrowly avoided disaster at LIV Golf UK on Thursday as a loose drive from Bryson DeChambeau nearly hit him in the head.

Veteran Poulter, 50, was left livid with his rival as he prepared to take his own shot on the fairway, but no 'fore' shout came from the American.

DeChambeau watched on as the Englishman turned around, raging, after the ball had landed around a metre from him.

Poulter gave a sarcastic shout of 'fore' in the direction of DeChambeau, after the crowd had reacted in shock after the Englishman narrowly avoided a nasty injury.

The ironic shout from Poulter was in reference to the shout golfers usually make when a ball is set to land near an opponent.

DeChambeau opted to slap his thigh in frustration at the JCB Golf and Country Club in Rocester.

A CRAZY moment in #LIVGolfUK as Ian Poulter is nearly hit by a Bryson DeChambeau tee-off 😱



📺 Watch LIV Golf live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/EywP5y88eu — TNT Sports (@tntsports) July 23, 2026

Bryson DeChambeau nearly hit Ian Poulter in the head with a wayward drive at LIV Golf

It had appeared, though, that no one told him his effort was heading for an opponent, and a calmer Poulter had that view when speaking about it after the day's play.

'It wasn't his fault at all,' he told TNT Sports. 'It just grazed the ear, I think on the way past, it was very close. It wouldn't have been good, it would have hurt - a lot.

'That was a shock to the system, the heart rate went up quite a bit. When you can hear that ball cutting through the air as it passes your ear.'

Commentators on the channel said: 'He didn't know, no one told him.

'You could tell Bryson was very sorry. No one told him. This is no one's fault here.'

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson and Dina Asher-Smith among NINE English call-offs in major blow for Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
The Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games suffered a major blow ahead of last night’s opening ceremony when nine English athletes pulled out on the eve of the event.

Heptathlete Katarina Johnson-Thompson and sprint star Dina Asher-Smith were the two leading lights to withdraw and they were joined by fellow Olympic medallists Matthew Hudson-Smith and Daryll Neita as well as 400m runner Amber Anning.

Hammer thrower Anna Purchase, middle distance runner Elliot Giles and sprinter Jona Efoloko also pulled out alongside steeplechaser Zac Seddon.

The loss of Olympic silver medallists Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith represents a significant blow to the competition’s organisers, with the former having been expected to target a hat-trick of Commonwealth Games titles having previously won gold in both Gold Coast and Birmingham.

Instead, she has chosen to prioritise the European Championships which are set to take place in Birmingham next month.

Johnson-Thompson has prioritised the upcoming European Championships in Birmingham

‘I’m gutted to have to pull out of this year’s Commonwealth Games,’ said Johnson-Thompson. ‘I was so looking forward to competing on home soil and having the chance to defend my Commonwealth title.

‘Although the injury I picked up earlier this season has improved, I haven’t been able to get back to the level I need to compete at my best.

‘After discussing it with my team, we’ve made the difficult decision to focus on giving myself the best chance of being ready for the European Championships. So I’m working very hard to be there later this season.

‘Missing a championship is never easy but I know it’s the right decision.’

The hectic schedule has presented a quandary for a number of leading athletes, including Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson, who decided not to pursue selection for the Glasgow Games.

Asher-Smith would have been one of the main draws in the women's relay event in Glasgow

International stars who have previously pulled out of the Games include multiple Olympic swimming medallists Kaylee McKeown and Summer McIntosh of Australia and Canada respectively, Hodgkinson’s 800m rival, Mary Moraa of Kenya, and St Lucia’s 100m Olympic champion Julien Alfred.

Away from the athletics track, triple Olympic gymnastics champion Max Whitlock was forced to call time on his comeback bid earlier this month due to injury.

These Games were supposed to be hosted by Australia in March, but the Victorian state pulled out due to budgetary pressure and Glasgow stepped in at late notice.

Sports.title: Chelsea close in on £55m agreement for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix as Arsenal announce £34m signing of Christos Tzolis: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fulham keeping an eye on young Real Madrid talent

Fulham have asked to be kept informed on a number of Real Madrid players, as has been widely reported, but among them is Thiago Pitarch.

At 18 years and 226 days, Pitarch became the club's youngest player to start twice in the Champions League knockout stages, surpassing Brazil forward Vinicius Jr's record by 10 days.

He impressed in Madrid's 3-0 win over Manchester City in March and has arrived back in training determined to impress Jose Mourinho and fight for a first team place.

Fulham have asked to be kept informed on a number of Real Madrid players, among them Thiago Pitarch

However, Alvaro Arbeloa is hoping that Mourinho decides a loan and season in the Premier League could prove more beneficial to his development. Fulham do face competition from other Spanish sides too.

Chelsea close in on £55m Maxence Lacroix

Chelsea are closing on agreement over a deal for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix worth around £55m.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Monday, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Chelsea are closing on agreement over a deal for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace locked in Matsima talks

Crystal Palace are continuing talks to sign centre-back Chrislain Matsima from Augsburg.

As negotiations carry on with Chelsea over the structure of a fee on the sale of Maxence Lacroix, Palace are looking to bolster their defensive options.

They have discussed Chelsea's Axel Disasi as an alternative too, but that is now seen as unlikely. The Frenchman had interest from Roma also.

They have already added versatile Oscar Mingueza on a free after he left Celta Vigo.

Gunners get their man

Arsenal have completed the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34million.

The fee is a record for the Belgian Pro League.

Arsenal have completed the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34million

The 24-year-old, formerly of Norwich City, scored 17 goals and added 23 assists in 36 league appearances last season.

Magpies swoop for £30m star

Newcastle United have agreed a £35.5million deal for Monaco midfielder Aladji Bamba.

The 20-year-old travelled to Tyneside for a medical on Thursday morning ahead of completing his surprise move.

The France U20 international has only had one season in Monaco's first team and has made only 12 competitive starts in all competitions but is rated as an outstanding prospect.

The clubs have agreed an initial £30m guaranteed payment plus £5.5m in add-ons. There is also a 15 percent sell-on clause in the agreement.

Bamba, who plays as a defensive midfielder, made five Champions League appearances and 18 in Ligue Un last season.

Newcastle sold Sandro Tonali to Tottenham last month and have been in the market for a second young midfielder after signing 18-year-old Sean Steur from Ajax. Another target, Freiburg's Johan Manzambi, opted to join Aston Villa instead last week after they had agreed a £49m fee. They also enquired about Tottenham’s £50m-rated Lucas Bergvall but insist stopped short of a formal offer.

Newcastle United have agreed a deal to sign Monaco defensive midfielder Aladji Bamba (left)

It underlines a change in strategy for Newcastle of signing players to develop which carries a degree of risk. It also gives added importance to keeping experienced players such as Bruno Guimaraes though he remains eager to leave for Arsenal.

Newcastle remain the market for another goalkeeper after moving on from Manchester City's James Trafford, who is destined for Leeds.

They did hold a meeting over Brighton's Carl Rushworth who has been the subject of offers from Coventry City and was also on Leeds' radar.

🚨 Newcastle have agreed a £30m deal with AS Monaco for Aladji Bamba



✈️ The 20-yr-old midfielder is due on Tyneside this morning — Craig Hope (@CraigHope_DM) July 23, 2026

Saints stand firm on Charles fee

Southampton risk pricing Shea Charles out of a move to the Premier League as they push for over £30million for the Northern Ireland international.

Fulham are the latest club to be rebuffed after they offered in the region of £24million for the 22-year-old.

The Cottagers believed they could strike a deal on the understanding Saints would accept £25m plus add-ons. However, the Championship side are demanding more.

Charles, who they bought from Manchester City in 2023, made 38 appearances last season and scored what looked to be the winning goal in the play-off semi-final against Middlesbrough only for the club to be excluded from the showpiece Wembley final as a consequence of 'Spygate', as exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport.

Leeds United had made the early running for Charles.

They also made three offers to Southampton which were subsequently rejected and are likely to consider other options.

Manchester City also hold a 15percent sell-on.

Saints are trying to build for the new season against the backdrop of head coach Tonda Eckert facing a suspension after he was charged with misconduct by the Football Association for his role in the Spygate scandal. He had until Tuesday to respond to the charges.

West Brom are also keen on Saints forward Cameron Archer.

Leeds in talks with City over Trafford move

Leeds United are in talks to sign England international goalkeeper James Trafford from Manchester City.

Trafford, who went to the World Cup this summer, only rejoined Manchester City from Burnley last summer but managed just four Premier League outings.

Leeds are on the hunt for a new No 1 goalkeeper after Karl Darlow left for Manchester United.

Trafford came through City's academy but, after making no first-team appearances, left for Burnley in 2023 after a series of loans.

He rejoined last summer in a £31million deal - a record sum for a British goalkeeper.

As Daily Mail Sport reported in April, Trafford was back on Newcastle United's agenda to be their number one but they were aware it as becoming increasingly difficult amid competition and valuation last week.

Leeds are acting are losing Darlow. Illan Meslier has also joined Arsenal while Torino want Lucas Perri.

They have asked about Zion Suzuki at Parma but are hopeful Trafford will join as he looks to cement his place as Jordan Pickford's main rival to the England number one jersey.

Aston Villa and Spurs have also shown interest in Trafford but he sees an opportunity at Leeds to build his future.

Newcastle have also met Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth’s representatives who remains subject of offers from Coventry City and was also on Leeds’ radar.

Leeds United are in talks to sign England international goalkeeper James Trafford (right)

Young Reds stopper leaves on loan

Liverpool goalkeeper Armin Pecsi has joined TSV Hartberg in Austria on a season-loan.

The 21-year-old, who made his senior international debut for Hungary last month, arrived at Anfield a year ago m.

He has been a regular for Liverpool's U21s and was also included in the senior side's matchday squad on five occasions.

Blues ramp up pursuit of Leverkusen teenager

Chelsea are stepping up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen winger Kerim Alajbegovic after offloading Alejandro Garnacho to Aston Villa and Nicolas Jackson expected to follow.

The exciting Bosnia international has had interest from Leeds United, Arsenal, Aston Villa and Atalanta.

Leverkusen sold the 18-year-old to Red Bull Salzburg last year but, after an impressive season, took up their option to buy him back this summer for £7million.

However, the winger made such an impression in Austria, and on World Cup duty with Bosnia, where he scored a spectacular long-range goal in their group-stage win over Qatar that his valuation is now closer to £30m.

Atalanta were considered to be in pole position earlier this month but Chelsea and Xabi Alonso were made aware of the opportunity and are now looking to strike a deal.

They have recognised the youngster's potential to add another pacy dimension to the first team set-up alongside new signing Morgan Rogers with Garnacho going and Nicolas Jackson expected to follow the Argentine to Villa.

Chelsea are stepping up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen winger Kerim Alajbegovic

Harrison poised for MLS return

Leeds United are finalising terms with New England Revolution for the sale of Jack Harrison.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this month the Revolution have been pursuing the 29-year-old this summer but were trying to navigate the required personal terms and fee.

The winger, who started his senior career with New York City, spent last season on loan at Fiorentina and has two years left on his contract at Elland Road.

Leeds are continuing negotiations with Manchester City over a fee for James Trafford.

The England goalkeeper is also expected to have a release clause in any contract he signs at Leeds.

City are also looking for a replacement should they agree terms.

Bettoni heads to Stamford Bridge

Chelsea have confirmed Harrison Bettoni has joined from Wigan Athletic on a four-year contract 2030.

The 18-year-old attacking midfielder was part of Wigan’s first team last season and appeared 27 times during a breakthrough campaign.

Chelsea beat off stern competition for his signature from Manchester City and AC Milan.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp officially named as Germany boss as worst-kept secret in football confirmed
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp officially named as Germany boss as worst-kept secret in football confirmed

Jurgen Klopp has been announced as the new Germany manager, succeeding Julian Nagelsmann following their embarrassment at the hands of Paraguay in the World Cup

View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp has been confirmed as the new Germany manager (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp has been officially announced as the new manager of Germany. The former Liverpool boss will leave his current role with Red Bull to succeed Julian Nagelsmann after his resignation in the wake of a disappointing World Cup.

‌



Klopp was identified as the top target immediately after Nagelsmann stepped down and agreed terms to take over earlier this month. The 59-year-old has been working as Red Bull's global head of soccer for the last 19 months following his departure from Liverpool in 2024, but will now step back into the dugout.

‌



Germany were knocked out of the World Cup in the last 32 by Paraguay, leaving Nagelsmann little choice but to resign the position he'd held since succeeding Hansi Flick in September 2023.

‌



Klopp, who has managed Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, was in North America following Die Mannschaft as a pundit for German TV, where he was critical of their approach. He stepped down at Liverpool at the end of the 2023/24 season due to fatigue but said earlier this month that he feels "recharged".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Argentina president goes on rant as calls for country to be banned from World Cup grow READ MORE :

Klopp won the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup and two League Cups during a hugely successful nine-year spell at Liverpool. He also has a stellar reputation in Germany, where he led Dortmund to two Bundesliga titles and the Champions League final.

‌



The move has been predicted for some time and has been an anticipated since Klopp publicly confirmed talks at the start of July, while working at the World Cup for a German broadcaster. "Yes, I can confirm the talks," Klopp told Magenta. "Things moved pretty quickly. Julian stepped down. The DFB are looking for a successor and they're talking to me.

"What needs to happen now? Time. I'm under contract with Red Bull. I've said I'm interested in the talks. They will be intensive because this isn't only about Julian Nagelsmann.

View 2 Images Julian Nagelsmann resigned after Germany were knocked out of the World Cup (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

‌



"I have an existing contract with Red Bull. I've said many times how much I enjoy this job. As a person, I usually honour contracts. But I've also made it clear that I'm interested in talks with the DFB.

"I also have to speak with (Red Bull CEO) Oliver Mintzlaff. He's my employer. We've already touched on a few things. I assume he won't stand in the way. I've been there for 19 months. It was an intense time.

"I'm ready. Once the talks begin, your mind starts racing. We have to change things fundamentally. There will have to be intensive discussions, because, of course, the problems we currently have cannot be pinned only on Julian Nagelsmann. Julian is an exceptional coach, and he will be able to prove that time and again throughout his coaching career."

Sports.title: Golf news: Rory McIlroy sends invite to Bryson DeChambeau as star withdraws from 3M Open
Sports.content:
Golf news: Rory McIlroy sends invite to Bryson DeChambeau as star withdraws from 3M Open

Golf news as Rory McIlroy reaches out to Bryson DeChambeau and major winner suffers another setback

View 3 Images Rory McIlroy has had plenty to say about Bryson DeChambeau (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

The golfing world continues to spin following an eventful Open Championship. Ryan Fox kept his head while all around him were losing theirs to make his major breakthrough at the age of 39 with a birdie at the last for a one-shot victory at Royal Birkdale.

‌



The New Zealander was one of only three players in the final 12 groups to shoot under par on a chaotic final day. The son of former All Blacks star Grant became his country's second Open champion after Sir Bob Charles in 1963.

‌



The Open also made the headlines for Bryson DeChambeau's conduct and Rory McIlroy's damning comments about the American. While McIlroy enjoys a break from the game, DeChambeau has stayed in the UK to play in the LIV Golf UK event at the JCB Country Club.

‌



Meanwhile, the PGA Tour continues with the 3M Open, where world number one Scheffler is part of the field. Here's a round-up of the latest golf news…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

McIlroy sends DeChambeau invite

McIlroy has sent a surprise invitation to DeChambeau despite his brutal comments about his conduct at The Open. The Masters champion let rip at DeChambeau after the LIV Golf star was docked two shots for a rules violation during his second round.

‌



Incensed by the punishment, DeChambeau requested to be driven out to the scene of the incident on the fifth hole, where he spent a lengthy period remonstrating with officials before returning to the scoring compound for further discussions.

Bryson DeChambeau controversy at The Open costs LIV Golf star more than £200,000 READ MORE :

The saga delayed the publication of the third-round tee times until around 11pm and prompted criticism from several players, including McIlroy, who accused DeChambeau of holding the tournament "hostage" and called his antics "performative." He also dropped in that he was "not particularly fond" of the 32-year-old.

Despite those words, McIlroy insists DeChambeau would be a welcome his addition to the field at September's Irish Open, which will be held at the Donald Trump-owned Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg.

‌



DeChambeau is friends with Trump and reportedly threatened to call the US President amid his spat with R&A officials at Birkdale. Therefore, there is speculation that he could make an appearance at the Irish Open, which would be welcomed by defending champion McIlroy, who said: "I mean, I think that would be great for the tournament, absolutely. Having someone like Bryson at the Irish Open, yeah, it would be great for the tournament."

View 3 Images DeChambeau could play at Donald Trump's course in Ireland (Image: Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images)

Day withdraws

Former world number one Jason Day has been forced to pull out of the 3M Open due to an ongoing back injury. The Australian, who missed the cut at The Open, withdrew during the first round of the US Open with a similar issue.

‌



He was replaced in the field at TPC ⁠Twin Cities in Minnesota by Charley Hoffman. Meanwhile, Scheffler made a strong start with a six-under par first round to sit three shots off the lead.

View 3 Images Jason Day's injury woes have continued (Image: Getty Images)

Scheffler, who finished tied fourth at Birkdale, began on the 10th and reached the turn at two under before picking up four more birdies in a blemish-free 65, holing 134 feet of putts in his first appearance at the tournament.

American Ben Kohles finished with an eagle three on the 18th to end two shots clear at the top of the leaderboard at nine under. Emiliano Grillo, Jackson Koivun and Gary Woodland, who hit rounds of 64, are in a share of second place.

Sports.content:
Is Tyson Fury fight on TV tonight? How to watch Mariusz Wach fight

Former heavyweight world champion Tyson Fury is staying active in the ring when he takes on Mariusz Wach this evening in his second fight in three months

View Image Tyson Fury and Mariusz Wach ahead of their fight (Image: Getty Images)

Sports.title: Tyson Fury issues yet another warning to rival Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury issues yet another warning to rival Anthony Joshua

View Image Tyson Fury fights tonight

Tyson Fury has warned Anthony Joshua he won't hang around waiting for their British mega-fight.

‌



Fury, 37, will return to the ring tonight to take on 46-year-old veteran Mariusz Wach in Thailand. He will then watch with his fingers crossed as Joshua attempts to keep his end of the bargain against Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia tomorrow evening. Routine victories for both men should leave the path clear to the belated settling of their decade-long heavyweight rivalry.

‌



But that showdown is without a date or venue and an impatient Fury insists he is ready to walk away. "I want to keep busy," he said. "I'm not banking on any fight happening or not happening I'm a fighter and I've never been able to stay busy; this is my second fight in two years. This year is the year of me staying busy and whatever happens I'm going to do that. Who knows, I might even have 10 fights this year."

‌



New venue emerges for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury mega-fight READ MORE :

Fury's meeting with Joshua was agreed earlier this year with Wembley chosen to play host in November. But broadcaster Netflix were spooked at the prospect of a mid-afternoon start on America’s west coast. Should the fight be held in the UK, the first bell could now ring as late - or as early - as 4am.

‌



But Las Vegas, Los Angeles and New York have now thrown their considerable hats into the ring. And even Joshua admits he could be powerless to prevent the Battle of Britain being shipped overseas. "Everyone controls a certain operation in the organisation and that is not my operation," he said.

"I am the landlord but, for example, my job is not to manage the staff rosters and what time they come in and who opens the store. So it's not my operation as to what time the fight will be." Saudi's boxing powerbroker Turki Al-Sheikh will ultimately decide the fate of the biggest fight in British boxing history.

And promoter Eddie Hearn added: "There was never any doubt this fight was in the UK until there were some approaches from America in terms of the revenue that could be achieved over there. When you sign a contract, you expect it to be honoured and followed but we’ve never done a deal with Turki where he hasn’t done that.

Article continues below

"I don’t think he’s trying to pull a fast one; he’s paying a lot of money for the fight, and he wants to make it as big a success for every stakeholder involved. If that means moving it to somewhere else, that's a conversation we'll have to have but we all hope, and we'd like to insist, that it’s in the UK.

"If it was the old days and the contract said the fight was in the UK, we wouldn't even be in a discussion. It would just be, 'Tough s***, mate, that’s what we signed, you're doing it.' But we also understand the relationship, and the fact there’s a lot of money in the fight."

Sports.title: Ibiza Final Boss' unlikely friendship with new mentor Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Ibiza Final Boss' unlikely friendship with new mentor Anthony Joshua

Ibiza Final Boss Jack Kay will be at Anthony Joshua's upcoming fight in Saudi Arabia and has shown a sneak peek into their bond as the internet sensation gets into boxing

View 4 Images Ibiza Final Boss is ready for another boxing bout (Image: Getty Images)

When Jack Kay headed out to Ibiza last year little did he know just how much his life was about to change. And now, the meme star is mixing it with some of the biggest names in music - and sport.

‌



He recently uploaded a video to social media of himself having a private video chat with none other than Anthony Joshua ahead of the heavyweight's bout this weekend's against Kristian Prenga. The Ibiza Final Boss was seen being mentored by champion AJ, who was giving him advice about his hopes in the boxing world.

‌



Kay appeared to be on holiday during the call as AJ was seen on his phone, with the pair sharing a laugh and AJ saying: "You've got some skills." Kay said he is "buzzing to go" ahead of his latest boxing contract after his debut win over Jordan McCann on a Misfits show.

‌



4 View 4 Images The Ibiza Final Boss speaking to Anthony Joshua (Image: jack.kayy1/Instagram) 4 View 4 Images AJ gave Kay some tips (Image: jack.kayy1/Instagram)

The Geordie is heard telling AJ: "I need to come and train with you boys," as the former heavyweight champion laughs and jokes it would be far too much for him.

"You'd die bro," AJ said. " Seriously, it's so hard." And Kay agreed, saying boxing "isn't for the faint hearted".

‌



The call went on, as the pair appeared to talk like pals. And the post was liked by big names in the DJ world such as fellow Geordie Patrick Topping, as well as Love Island's Adam Collard.

Kay captioned his upload: "Good to get some education of the main man @anthonyjoshua. He’s going to help me takeover @misfitsboxing let’s go."

Kay later told DAZN Boxing that Joshua invited him to his upcoming fight in Saudi Arabia and took him up on his offer. "Yeah, I'll be over there," he said with a smile.

‌



Opening up on how the friendship started, he confessed it was "through a friend through a friend sort to speak". He added in a message to the former champ: "AJ, you're going to smash him. You're the man. Bring it home."

View 4 Images AJ is ready for his next fight (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



Kay became an internet sensation last summer after a video of him dancing in Ibiza went viral. He became known as the 'Ibiza Final Boss' after videos of him dancing the night away whilst holidaying in the party hotspot. His lego style hair do, massive sunglasses and distinct moves on the dance floor that captured serious attention.

While many thought he would just be an overnight success and fizzle out, it appears he is here to stay and ready to make a name for himself in Misfits boxing. After receiving a reported £50,000 for his first bout, it's said he is now in a five-fight deal with the promoter, with his pay packet set to dramatically increase.

In a recent Channel 4 documentary, Kay, who now drives a £55,000 Range Rover SVR, shared how he was keen to bring in as much money as he could for the sake of his daughter. He explained: "I'm trying to keep myself on a level head with it because I've got a little daughter back home, I had nothing growing up, so to give her the life when she's older, she can have anything she wants, is just unbelievable."

Article continues below

He has enjoyed a year of mixing it with the stars and his latest call shows just how his life has changed.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
