World.title: Ukraine hits ‘Russia’s Amazon’ warehouses outside St Petersburg
World.content:
Saint Petersburg – Ukrainian drones Friday hit warehouses for Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries for a third time in six days, this time near Saint Petersburg, triggering a fire that sent smoke pouring over the historic city.

Kyiv has accused Wildberries — Russia’s largest online retailer often known as the Russian equivalent of Amazon — of storing drone parts and helping the Russian army.

Ukraine has targeted Saint Petersburg as it steps up long-range drone strikes on Russian energy, military and logistics sites in recent weeks, calling the attacks justified retribution for Moscow’s nightly drone and missile barrage of its cities.

Russia’s defence ministry said its forces shot down some 571 drones overnight over more than a dozen regions and Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that Russia annexed in 2014 — one of the largest one-night barrages of the war.

In Saint Petersburg, an AFP reporter saw grey smoke rising into the morning sky over high-rise residential buildings in the city, President Vladimir Putin’s hometown that is more than 800 kilometres (500 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

Wildberries said two of its logistics facilities in Saint Petersburg and one in Simferopol, in Moscow-annexed Crimea, were hit.

“Rapid evacuation was carried out at all the warehouses … according to preliminary data, there are no casualties,” Wildberries CEO Tatyana Kim said on social media.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of the surrounding Leningrad region said three people were wounded in the attack, which saw at least 59 drones fired towards Saint Petersburg.

It was the third overnight attack by Ukraine on Wildberries’ sites in the past week.

Last weekend, eight night-shift workers were killed in attacks on Wildberries sites that saw one of the company’s main warehouses outside Moscow burn to the ground.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alleged after the first attack that the facilities were used to “supply sanctioned components for drone production and navigation equipment.”

Hundreds of small businesses saw their inventories wiped out in the strike, triggering angry comments on social media.

Kyiv calls its strikes “long-range sanctions”, saying the attacks are justified retribution for Russia’s more than four-year offensive and nightly attacks on its cities.

The campaign has triggered nationwide fuel shortages and, Kyiv says, dented Russia’s financial war chest.

– ‘Escalation’ –

Columns of thick black smoke were still billowing into the sky from one of the factories hours after the hit, an AFP reporter saw.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spent the first years of the war trying to shield the population from the fall-out of his decision to launch the offensive on Ukraine.

But the strikes on oil refineries have triggered fuel shortages and big attacks near major cities have brought the dramatic visible consequences of the war into the homes of many Russians.

Firefighters and investigators had been deployed to the sites in Saint Petersburg as the blaze raged through the morning, Russian officials said.

Saint Petersburg’s Pulkovo airport suspended flights during the attack, resuming operations around 06:00 (0300 GMT), with around 50 departures disrupted.

Both Russia and Ukraine have escalated their long-range strikes in recent months.

Moscow’s forces have fired increasing numbers of ballistic missiles at Kyiv — killing dozens and ripping open apartment blocks.

US President Donald Trump has appeared to give his backing to Ukraine’s counter-attacks on Russia — calling the strikes “an escalation that can lead to an end”.

Washington’s attempts to mediate a peace deal between the warring sides have largely stalled with its own war on Iran raging.

The United Nations has reported a surge in civilian deaths in 2026, saying June was the deadliest month since mid-2022.

Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and tens of thousands of civilians have been killed since Russia launched its full-scale offensive in February 2022 — though there is no precise toll with neither side routinely revealing the number of their losses.

World.title: South Korean tycoon ordered to pay $644m in divorce
World.content:
Seoul – A South Korean court ordered an AI chip-manufacturing tycoon on Friday to make a trimmed-down $644 million divorce payment to his former wife.

Chey Tae-won, 65, is the chairman of the SK Group, which owns world-leading memory chipmaker SK hynix — a pillar of South Korea’s tech-led economy.

Seoul High Court in 2024 had told him to pay 1.38 trillion won ($940 million) to his ex-wife Roh Soh-yeong, daughter of a former South Korea president.

The sum — equal to more than $1 billion at the exchange rate at the time of the ruling — led local media to dub it the “divorce of the century”.

Chey appealed to the Supreme Court, which told the high court to reconsider its 2024 decision and led to the tycoon’s reduced divorce bill of 944 billion won ($644 million).

The settlement is not yet final, however, as either side may refer it back to the Supreme Court.

The acrimonious case centres on the definition and valuation of the couple’s shared assets, including Chey’s lucrative stake in the SK Group.

Seoul High Court ruled Friday that Roh was entitled to a cash payout worth one-third of the couple’s marital assets.

“The defendant’s shareholdings increased substantially during the marriage through his management activities,” the court said.

“The plaintiff contributed to that increase through homemaking, childcare and public-facing activities related to SK Group.”

Chey and Roh married in 1988, but the couple are believed to have lived apart for more than 15 years. In 2015 he admitted to fathering a child with his lover.

With SK hynix selling vital memory chips to AI computing company Nvidia, Chey’s stake is now worth roughly $5.5 billion, according to regulatory filings and public data.

Roh, 65, has three children with Chey and has built a career in the cultural space, running a digital art museum.

– Bribes –

The pair were wed in Seoul’s presidential Blue House when her father Roh Tae-woo led the country from 1988 to 1993.

They have battled over the split in the courts since 2022, after Chey filed for divorce in 2017 and mediation broke down.

The court’s original 2024 ruling ordering the payout to Roh cited a 30 billion won slush fund her ex-president father used to propel SK Group’s growth.

The court said at the time that could be counted as her contribution towards the couple’s shared assets.

But in October last year the Supreme Court quashed that argument, saying that any such cash likely stemmed from illegal bribes and therefore should not be counted.

Another question was whether the dramatic increase in SK Group’s value since the couple’s separation, on the cusp of the AI boom, should be reflected in the asset division.

“The court took into account the sharp rise in the value of the defendant’s shareholdings when determining the property division ratio,” Friday’s court statement said.

SK Group shares have more than tripled in value since December 2015, when Chey publicly disclosed his extramarital affair.

The Supreme Court had already separately ordered Chey to make an alimony payment to Roh of 2 billion won.

World.title: PepsiCo deepens Iraq partnership with manufacturing, agriculture deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – PepsiCo has inked agreements with two Iraqi partners to increase food and beverage production, boost agricultural supply chains, and create employment, adding to a string of US investments announced during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington.

The agreements, inked during the U.S.-Iraq High-Level Business Summit organized by the US Chamber of Commerce, strengthen PepsiCo’s collaborations with Baghdad Soft Drinks Company (BSDC), its long-standing bottling partner in Iraq, and Green Iraq Company (GICO).

According to the deal with BSDC, PepsiCo will aim to increase yearly production capacity to more than 250 million beverage cases, maintaining Iraq’s position as one of the company’s major manufacturing and bottling centers in the Middle East.

The expansion is planned to create new employment in manufacturing, engineering, logistics, and distribution, as well as teach and provide technical skills to Iraqi engineers and technicians.

A separate deal with GICO seeks to increase food production capacity and agricultural productivity by bringing advanced irrigation methods and farming practices to local farmers, therefore boosting Iraq’s goal to become a regional food and beverage export center.

According to PepsiCo, the program aims to boost domestic supply chains by encouraging more local procurement and assisting Iraqi farmers in improving yields and sustainability.

The deals were part of a series of commercial understandings struck at the summit, in which US and Iraqi firms announced commitments in energy, banking, aviation, infrastructure, and manufacturing as Baghdad strives to diversify its economy away from oil and attract foreign investment.

Baghdad Soft Drinks Company has been working with PepsiCo for over four decades, and both agreements were signed on behalf of BSDC and GICO by majority stakeholder Tarek Al Hassan.

The investment demonstrates global firms’ rising interest in Iraq’s consumer products industry, as improved economic circumstances and government reforms stimulate more private sector investment and industrial growth.

World.title: Socceroos star Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine
World.content:
Sydney – Australian World Cup star Cristian Volpato allegedly tested positive for cocaine after he was pulled over for speeding in Sydney on Friday, police and reports said.

A New South Wales police statement said a 22-year-old man — widely identified as Italy-based Volpato by local media — was allegedly caught speeding twice overnight.

He passed a roadside breath test on the first occasion and was issued an infringement notice before being pulled over again two hours later.

This time he was drug tested and returned a positive result for cocaine, police claimed, with a second sample sent for further analysis.

“His international driver’s licence was suspended for a period of six months, withdrawing his driving privileges in NSW,” police said.

Volpato, who plays for Serie A side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup after switching his international allegiance from Italy to Australia shortly before the tournament.

He was born and raised in Sydney before moving overseas and represented Italy at various youth levels.

Tony Basha, a Sydney-based coach who trained Volpato before he moved to Italy and remains a mentor, told the Sydney Morning Herald the attacking midfielder denied taking cocaine or any other illicit substance.

“He was adamant he didn’t touch it,” Basha said. “He was shocked. I’m shocked because it’s a big allegation.”

World.title: Volkswagen profit plunges as carmaker weighs mass job cuts
World.content:
Frankfurt – Volkswagen said Friday that its net profit plunged in the second quarter as the crisis-hit carmaker, weighing up to 100,000 job cuts worldwide, grapples with increasing competition in and from China.

Net profit for the three months to the end of June came in at 1.54 billion euros ($1.75 billion), the 10-brand group said, a fall of 32.9 percent on the same period last year. Last year’s figure was itself a decline of almost 37 percent on 2024.

The result was hit by a 500-million-euro charge the carmaker booked for stopping US production of its electric ID.4, Volkswagen said, as well as “negative mix effects”, meaning the automotive giant sold more lower-margin products.

The firm, which in addition to its own brand also includes the likes of Lamborghini, Audi, Skoda and Porsche, also cut its guidance for the year and said it now saw sales flat or falling up to three percent. It previously expected growth of up to three percent.

The results pile pressure on the beleaguered group, which has been suffering from slimmer margins from the sales of electric cars, US tariffs and above all intense Chinese competition.

“We must accelerate efforts to structurally lower our cost base and sustainably improve our earnings quality,” Volkswagen finance chief Arno Antlitz said. “What matters now is swift and consistent implementation.”

World.title: Iraq border in focus as Kuwait reports drone attack
World.content:
Dubai – Here are the main events related to the war in the Middle East:

– Iran blasts Trump assets threat –

Tehran said Friday that US President Donald Trump’s threat to pay for shipping damage with Iranian assets was an “incendiary precedent”.

Trump had said that Washington would start using frozen Iranian assets “that the United States has in its possession, and controls” to pay for “any and all damages done to Ships, Cargo or anything related” in the region.

– New US strikes –

The United States military said Thursday it was attacking Iran for the 13th night in a row, adding that strikes were aimed at military targets with the goal of diminishing Iranian ability to attack shipping.

Iranian state media reported that US missiles had hit the city of Ahvaz, near the border with Iraq, and explosions were heard in the port city of Bandar Abbas on the Strait of Hormuz and in Omidiyeh.

– Kuwait under attack –

Kuwaiti air defences have opened fire on incoming Iranian missiles and drones, hours after reporting a new drone attack at the border crossing with Iraq.

“Kuwaiti air defences are currently intercepting hostile missile and drone attacks following the wrongful Iranian aggression,” the general staff said in a message posted on social media.

– Trump rebuked –

The US House of Representatives passed a largely symbolic resolution calling for President Donald Trump to halt military action against Iran, delivering another congressional rebuke as the Middle East war escalates.

The measure directs Trump to remove US forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress explicitly authorises the war.

– Houthi attacks ‘illegal’ –

Attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea by Yemen’s Houthi militants have drawn condemnation from around Europe.

Germany said the attacks risked escalating conflicts, Britain condemned the group’s “reckless actions” and EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas said the attacks were “unacceptable” and “illegal”.

– UN chief warning –

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said the Middle East conflict was “getting out of control”.

“It is teetering on the edge of the unimaginable,” he said.

– Oil passes $100 –

The price of the benchmark international oil contract, Brent North Sea soared more than eight percent to reach $101.93 a barrel after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck oil tankers in the Red Sea.

The main US oil contract, West Texas Intermediate, rose 7.6 percent to $93.44 a barrel.

– Island strike –

Iranian news outlet Tasnim reported that a US missile had hit a site near the town of Suza on Qeshm Island, in the disputed Strait of Hormuz.

– Trump threatens Houthis –

Trump threatened Yemen’s Houthi rebels with “major military punishment” after they launched missile and drone strikes at oil tankers in the Red Sea.

“The US will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis themselves” should the rebels launch further attacks, Trump said on his Truth Social network.

– Britain withdraws Iran staff –

Britain said it had withdrawn remaining diplomatic staff from Iran.

“Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran. Our embassy continues to operate remotely,” the foreign ministry said on its website.

World.title: Kuwait blames Iran afters drones hit border with Iraq
World.content:
Kuwait City — Kuwait on Thursday said drones hit its side of the border with Iraq, with one Kuwaiti official telling AFP Iran was to blame.

“The Al-Abdali border crossing was attacked this afternoon by hostile drones, resulting in material damage, but thankfully no casualties,” defense ministry spokesman Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan said in a statement.

An Iraqi security source also confirmed the incident prior to the ministry’s statement.

World.title: Iraq, Iran sign transport, rail deals after Tehran talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq and Iran inked an agreement and three memorandums of understanding on transportation, rail connection, and government collaboration as Prime Minister Ali al-Falih al-Zaidi wrapped up an official visit to Tehran aimed at improving bilateral relations.

According to the Iraqi Prime Minister’s office, Al-Zaidi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and conducted extensive conversations with key Iranian officials such as Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Judiciary Chief Gholam-Hossein Mohseni Eje’i.

The two sides signed an agreement on international road freight transport and shipping, as well as memorandums of understanding to extend a railway connecting Kermanshah, Khosravi, Khanqin, and Baghdad, establish a twinning agreement between Baghdad and Tehran municipalities, and collaborate on government administration and human resource training.

Iraqi ministers in charge of foreign affairs, electricity, and finance, as well as the head of the Planning Commission, signed the agreements in the presence of Al-Zaidi and Pezeshkian.

The proposed railway extension would improve overland transportation links between Iraq and Iran, as part of Baghdad’s larger plans to expand regional trade corridors and improve cross-border connectivity through investments in rail, road, and logistics infrastructure.

The visit takes place as Iraq aims to retain tight economic and political connections with neighboring Iran while simultaneously developing partnerships with the United States and Gulf nations as part of a larger drive to diversify investment and boost regional cooperation.

According to the New York Times, Iran rejected a US cease-fire proposal delivered by Al-Zaidi during the visit, while Iraqi authorities made no public comment on the claim.

World.title: Neet's top 2 scorers: Protest is a right, reform is the answer
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Aryan Gupta and Panshul Bansal felt the same anger and sense of injustice as lakhs of

aspirants when the May-3 examination was cancelled after a paper leak. They believe students were within their rights to protest.

But instead of joining the demonstrations, they stepped away from the noise, revitalised their will and prepared for the June 21 re-examination â a decision that took them to the top.

Both scored 715 out of 720, with Gupta securing All India Rank 1 and Bansal placed second under the tie-break rule. They now want computer-based testing (CBT), tighter security and two NEET attempts a year to help examinees avoid what they experienced this year.

âAlthough it was unfair, it was not unfair only to me. It was unfair to everyone,â Gupta said, adding that he treated the re-test as a chance to improve his performance. He had expected around 696 marks in the first examination. The cancellation left him âdevastated and disappointedâ, but he focused on what remained in his control.

Bansal did the same. As reports about the leak and protests multiplied, he stopped following the news for nearly two months because it was giving him ânegative thoughtsâ.





But both defended studentsâ right to demonstrate. âProtest and dissent are basic rights of a citizen. They are very essential for a democracy,â Gupta said. Bansal said his job was to prepare, while it was govtâs responsibility to repair the system.

Their re-examination experience was better. Gupta said the June-21 test was conducted in a âmuch more secure and much better mannerâ, with police, an ambulance and firefighters at his centre.

During the first test, invigilators kept speaking and shouting for nearly two hours. âDuring the second examination, decorum was maintained,â he said.

Both support shifting NEET from pen-and-paper mode to CBT. Gupta said it would reduce risks linked to transporting papers and eliminate OMR mistakes.

Bansal suggested the same to Dharmendra Pradhan during his meeting with the Union education minister. CBT would not be foolproof because cybersecurity risks remained, he said, but would be safer than a paper system involving many handlers. âSomeone only needs to corrupt one person in that chain,â he said.

The two also want NEET twice a year, like JEE Main. âEverything cannot be decided by what happens during a single three-hour examination,â Gupta said, citing his improved performance despite largely unchanged preparations.

World.title: SC proposes special courts for Manipur violence cases; directs CBI, SIT to expedite investigations
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday proposed setting up special courts to conduct day-to-day trials in criminal cases arising from the 2023 ethnic violence in Manipur, while directing investigating agencies to expedite pending probes and ensure victims receive copies of chargesheets without delay.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted that many victims and their families were yet to receive copies of chargesheets filed by the CBI and the Manipur Special Investigation Team (SIT).

The court allowed legal aid counsel representing the victims to approach the offices of the Chief Justices of the Gauhati high court and the Manipur high court to obtain copies of the chargesheets.

Gives directions to CBI, SIT

The Bench also asked additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, the CBI, the SIT and the Manipur government, to furnish details of cases where investigations have been completed and chargesheets filed, as well as cases where the probe is still pending.

The information, the court said, would help determine how many special courts are required to conduct speedy trials in the violence-related cases.





The Supreme Court further directed the Manipur High Court to examine cases relating to 30 persons who have remained missing since the ethnic clashes began.

It also asked the CBI, the state SIT and the court-appointed monitoring committee headed by former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar to file fresh status reports on the progress of investigations.

More than 200 people have been killed, hundreds injured and thousands displaced since ethnic violence erupted in Manipur on May 3, 2023, following a 'Tribal Solidarity March' organised in the hill districts to protest the Meitei community's demand for Scheduled Tribe (ST) status.

World.title: Uttarakhand Technical University cancels two exams after alleged paper leak, one arrested
World.content:
Students protest after Uttarakhand Technical University cancelled two BTech exams upon a paper leak allegation. (Photo: Agencies)

DEHRADUN: An alleged paper leak surfaced at Veer Madho Singh Bhandari Uttarakhand Technical University (UTU) on Thursday, prompting the university administration to cancel two B. Tech semester examinations.The Dehradun Police has registered an FIR and arrested Ashish Kumar Gupta, an Assistant Professor at Shivalik College of Engineering, who was a member of the team responsible for setting the question paper for the subject Machine Learning for Internet of Things.Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Dehradun, Pramendra Dobhal, said that accused Ashish Gupta breached confidentiality.The probe revealed that several questions in the examination matched those that had been shared earlier in a WhatsApp group associated with the college. Based on the complaint, an FIR (Case No. 144/26) was registered at Premnagar Police Station under Sections 316 (criminal breach of trust), 318(4) (cheating), and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The police officer said, "Vinay Kumar Patel, the Examination Controller of Uttarakhand Technical University, filed a complaint with Prem Nagar Police Station alleging that the question paper for internal exams scheduled for July 7 and 8 was leaked by a hired professor to benefit certain individuals, thereby breaching exam confidentiality.""Immediately upon receiving the complaint, Prem Nagar Police registered a case, gathered relevant information, and included an internal investigation report. The main accused, Ashish Gupta, was arrested, and all documents related to the exam preparations and the leaked question paper were seized. Gupta will be presented in court, and anyone found to have benefited unfairly from the leaked paper will also be included in the investigation," the SSP added.He said, "The action is in accordance with the directives of the Chief Minister, ensuring that any irregularities are promptly addressed with strong legal action."This paper leak controversy comes amid widespread protests over the NEET-UG paper leak, which happened in May, after which the re-examination was held on June 21.

World.title: 'There is such a thing as optics too': Opposition reacts to Sonam Wangchuk ending hunger strike
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders on Friday reacted to activist

ending his 26-day hunger strike, which he had undertaken in support of students protesting the alleged NEET-UG examination irregularities and demanding accountability from the Centre.

AAP national convenor

welcomed Wangchuk's decision to call off his 'anshan' citing that his life is important for the nation.

In an X post, Kejriwal also urged people to participate in the nationwide protests announced by the Cockroach Janta Party (

).

Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut said Wangchuk ending his fast was a matter of joy but questioned the circumstances under which it concluded.

"Sonam Wangchuk ending his 26-day hunger strike is a matter of joy.

But it would have been far better if it had been called off by one of the girls who were beaten during the protest. And if he had ended it from the very same stage at Jantar Mantar from where you were dragged away, it would have been even more meaningful. Anyway! The people are wise," Raut wrote.

TMC MP Mahua Moitra also thanked Wangchuk for his efforts but maintained that the Centre's assurances were insufficient.

"Dear @Wangchuk66, thank you for your efforts. Shri JP Nadda and Dr.





Jitendra Singh's platitudes may pacify you but nothing short of Pradhan's resignation will suffice for the youth of this country," she said in a post on X.

In a separate post, Moitra appeared to question the optics surrounding the end of the hunger strike, writing in Hindi: "Today if there was, then from someone else's hand they'd snatch it away, sir... there is such a thing as optics too... :-)"

Wangchuk ended his fast earlier on Friday at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, after the Centre agreed to hold talks with the CJP at a neutral venue. The CJP has said its nationwide protests will continue until its key demandsâincluding the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for affected families and withdrawal of cases against protestersâare met.

World.title: 'Will monitor throughout the year': SC assures 'institutionalisation' of NEET reforms
World.content:
CJP supporters raise slogans during a protest demanding the Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation NEET irregularities. (PTI photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view Would you advocate for more stakeholder involvement in the NEET-UG reform process? Yes, it's crucial for success No, it complicates decisions 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Friday directed the central government to file a detailed affidavits on the "progress made in the implementaion" of reforms meant to address NEET-UG paper leak.The court said that it will "closely monitor" the progress "throughout the year" to ensure "institutionalisation takes place". The top court has also asked the National Testing Agency (NTA) to file the affidavits.A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the affidavit must explain the steps taken to institutionalise the reforms instead of relying on ad hoc measures.Justice Narasimha noted that the deployment of the Indian Air Force (for safe transportation of questions) after the paper leak was only an ad hoc measure and could not be a permanent solution."We will closely monitor it. We will ensure institutionalisation takes place. We will monitor it throughout the year", the Court said while posting the matter for next Monday.The court, according to news agency ANI, also sought details on the proposed governing board, expert-led units, stakeholder nominations and the implementation of the High-Powered Committeeâs recommendations across ten verticals, including digital infrastructure, security, research and development, transparency, administration and human resources.It also asked the Centre to explain the role and progress of the newly appointed Additional Directors General for security, monitoring and vigilance. The bench also sought a status report on reforms at every stage of the examination cycle â pre-exam, during the exam and post-exam.The top court has asked the Centre to explain the progress made on testing modalities with State and district authorities, multiple-session examinations, examination centres, question papers, printing and transportation.The Court also sought details on the proposal to shift to Computer-Based Testing and the safeguards for data protection.The Court also asked the Centre to explain its proposal on technologies such as DigiYatra for candidate verification.Observing that the Unionâs affidavit has not addressed these issues, the Court accepted Solicitor General Tushar Mehtaâs assurance that a fresh affidavit would be filed.

World.title: Khalistani terror suspect, US national held while entering India from Nepal
World.content:
The two men were identified as Vikramjit Singh, who is wanted in connection with a 2023 case registered at Ajnala police station in Punjab, and Manveer Singh Dhillon, a US national originally from Punjab's Moga district.

NEW DELHI: A wanted member of the pro-Khalistan outfit Waris Punjab De and a US national linked to the organisation were arrested while allegedly attempting to enter India from Nepal through the Indo-Nepal border in Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich district, police said on Thursday. PTI reported.Bahraich Superintendent of Police Vishwajeet Srivastava said the arrests were made during a joint operation by the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and the Uttar Pradesh Police at the Rupaidiha border under the Rupaidiha police station area.The two men were identified as Vikramjit Singh, who is wanted in connection with a 2023 case registered at Ajnala police station in Punjab, and Manveer Singh Dhillon, a US national originally from Punjab's Moga district.According to police, Vikramjit had been absconding in the Punjab case, while Dhillon is suspected to have entered Nepal before attempting to cross into India without a valid Indian visa in an effort to avoid the attention of law enforcement agencies. The duo was intercepted after crossing the Rupaidiha border post, where verification and questioning allegedly revealed their identities and links to Waris Punjab De.Police have registered a case against both men under relevant provisions at the Rupaidiha police station. Officials from multiple security and intelligence agencies also questioned the accused following their detention.Three Indian nationals were also arrested for allegedly facilitating the pair's illegal entry into India. They were identified as Suresh Kumar Pathak and Dilip Upadhyay, both residents of Rupaidiha town, and Rahul Kumar, who was allegedly driving the vehicle arranged for the two men.The arrests come just weeks after another US national, Jordan Brown, was detained near the India-Nepal border in Maharajganj while allegedly attempting to cross into Nepal without valid travel documents.

World.title: Crackdown on paper leak: Govt planning to tweak anti-cheating law by increasing jail term
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The central government will introduce an amendment to the law meant to prevent paper leaks and cheating in public examinations to provide for fast-track courts for paper leak cases.

In the expected amendment, the government is also likely to increase the jail term for offenders from the current 10-year maximum, sources told TOI. The proposed bill will be taken up by the Cabinet this afternoon.

The jail terms in the existing Act will be increased across three sections and fast track courts will be made mandatory for trial in the Bill in all such cases.

The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, which was enacted to curb paper leaks, cheating and organised malpractices in public examinations such as UPSC, SSC and NTA tests, provides for penalties, including up to 10 years' imprisonment and a Rs 1 crore fine.

The proposed Bill is in line with PM Modi's late Thursday announcement that the Union Cabinet will on Friday discuss a Bill to further strengthen the anti-cheating law and ensure stricter punishment for offenders.

Hours after ordering the establishment of fast-track courts, in a recorded message posted on social media at midnight, PM said that based on the discussion a bill will be moved on Monday, when the second week of the current Parliament session begins, and government will seek its passage at the earliest.





âFast-track courts and strict punishment will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow and it will be given final shape after the discussion,â Modi said, while underlining that government has been working on addressing the concerns related to medical entrance exams paper leak over the last two and a half months. He said that government had so far focused on ensuring that students did not lose a year and decided to conduct exams for 22 lakh students, using âall its mightâ, with results also declared.

Modiâs message through the unusual mode came minutes after government replaced the education secretary amid the ongoing protests against the

paper leak.

Poll Vote & Share your view What measure should be prioritized to prevent exam paper leaks? Stricter laws Better technology More awareness campaigns 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Over the last two days, officials said, PMO has been engaged with the education ministry over the NEET exam, retest and K Radhakrishnan committee on NTA reforms, with over two dozen queries flowing from Seva Teerth.

World.title: ‘No plans to enter airline business:’ Adani Group
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has denied any plans to enter the airline business. An

Limited spokesperson said on Friday: âWe would like to categorically deny the recent media reports and market speculation suggesting that Adani Enterprises is planning to launch an airline.

These reports are entirely baseless and factually incorrect. Adani Enterprises is not evaluating any proposal to enter the airline business.â

The statement comes amid govt being reportedly being uncomfortable with a country of the size and economic potential of India having a duopoly of airlines â IndiGo and Tataâs Air India group. Akasa is also coming up in a big way. However, the West Asia crisis coupled with other India-specific issues like closure of Pakistan airspace and the rupeeâs relentless crash have made things tougher for airlines here than they are for carriers globally.

Both IndiGo and AI Group have slashed flights due to escalating operational costs. Smaller players like SpiceJet are struggling to survive.

In this context, India is considering ways to make it easier to launch new airlines. One of these steps reportedly were allowing the operators of Indiaâs busiest airports â Delhi and Mumbai â to hold more than 10% stake in airlines. The GMR and Adani groups run these two hubs, respectively.





Both these conglomerates have major presence in aviation that goes beyond just running airports as they have maintenance, repair overhaul (MRO) and other businesses.

The Adani Group has tied up with Embraer to make-in-India regional jets. However, the Brazilian aerospace company has linked setting up and operationalising the proposed final assembly line (FAL) to getting a firm order of at least 200 jets. Dholera in Gujarat has been selected as the site for this proposed FAL.

Billionaire Gautam Adani-led conglomerate is the biggest private airport operator in India (in terms of number of airports). It operates hubs in Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Jaipur, Guwahati, Mangalore and Thiruvananthapuram.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim strike on U.S. tech giant Amazon’s data centre in Bahrain
World.content:
Iran Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Friday (July 24, 2026) that Iran would hold accountable any country assisting the United States in an attack on the Islamic republic.

“Any participation, cooperation or assistance in committing aggression against Iran will create international responsibility for the relevant parties,” Mr. Araghchi said at a meeting in Kyrgyzstan, adding that Iran “reserves its right to take all necessary measures within the framework of self-defence”.

Also read: Houthi attack on Saudi tankers drives Brent past $100 per barrel, stresses India’s crude routes

Meanwhile, Bahrain’s Interior Ministry said sirens sounded across the country on Friday, as a media correspondent reported hearing an explosion amid renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities that have triggered near-daily Iranian attacks on the island kingdom.

The Houthis threatened to shut down another key trade route, with the world economy already reeling from Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran and the U.S. have stepped up attacks as they vie for control of the strait, through which a fifth of the world’s oil and gas transited in peacetime, setting off a scramble for alternative routes.

Also read: Iran vows to continue strikes in West Asia war

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Talks under way between CJP and Union Ministers
World.content:
The government and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held talks on Friday (July 24, 2026) at the Constitution Club of India after the Centre “agreed” to the CJP’s demand that the meeting be held at a neutral venue.

The CJP has said the “strictest action” the government could take against examination irregularities was to remove Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement that a Bill providing for stringent action against paper leaks would be introduced in Parliament.

Also Read: PM reaches out to students; Sonam Wangchuk ends fast

The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) is “verifying media reports” on the use of pellet guns by the Rapid Action Force (RAF) against unarmed protesters during July 20 march to Parliament in New Delhi, an official said on Friday (July 24, 2026). This comes three days after The Hindu reported the first known instance of security forces using pellet guns on civilians in the national capital.

Also Read: Student protests are the consequence of Modi government’s policies, writes Sonia Gandhi

Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his indefinite hunger strike after the government assured him that his demands would be met. He announced the end of his fast after Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at the Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around Thursday (July 23, 2026) midnight and conveyed the government’s assurances.

World.title: Kerala govt forms high-level panel to draft Sidharthan Anti-Ragging and Student Welfare Act
World.content:
Kerala State Higher Education Council vice-chairperson Achuthsankar S. Nair will chair the high-level committee constituted to prepare the draft legislation of the proposed Sidharthan Anti-Ragging and Student Welfare Act and Sidharthan Student Distress App to strengthen anti-ragging measures in educational institutions in the State.

The committee, constituted by the Home Department, has been tasked with consolidating expert opinions and drafting comprehensive legislative proposals to establish emergency digital reporting, institutionalise mental health support, and enforce strict safety guidelines across school and college campuses.

Minhaj Alam, Additional Chief Secretary of the Home Department, will serve as the convenor of the committee.

The other members of the panel include B. Ashok, Principal Secretary, Higher Education Department; Sharmila Mary Joseph, Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department; K. G. Sanalkumar, Secretary, Law Department; Abdul Nasar B., Special Secretary, Social Justice Department; and Arul R. B. Krishna, District Police Chief, Thiruvananthapuram City.

Shijida Shain (Assistant Professor, University College of Engineering, Karyavattom; Kiran P.S., State Nodal Officer, State Mental Health Program; Ranjith Balan, Chief Executive Officer, Doubtbox Edutainment Pvt. Ltd.; legal expert Y. Vinod Kumar, M.J. Yadukrishnan, a public representative from Kollam have also been included in the committee.

The legislative initiative, which was announced in the revised State Budget, also comes against the backdrop of a writ petition filed by the Kerala State Legal Services Authority (KeLSA) that expressed severe concern over the escalating cruelty of ragging incidents in educational institutions.

While reviewing the petition, the Kerala High Court observed that despite the Kerala Prohibition of Ragging Act having been enacted 27 years ago, the failure to frame the necessary rules had severely weakened law enforcement capabilities. Consequently, the court directed the State government to constitute a multi-disciplinary working group to evaluate necessary amendments and draft actionable rules.

World.title: Delhi HC declines interim injunction against OpenAI in ANI copyright suit
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday (July 24, 2026) refused to grant interim relief to news agency Asian News International (ANI) in its copyright infringement suit against OpenAI, holding prima facie that the company’s use of ANI’s works for training ChatGPT falls within the exception under Section 52(1)(a) of the Copyright Act.

Justice Amit Bansal said OpenAI’s act of storing ANI’s literary works for training its Large Language Models (LLMs), prima facie, did not amount to copyright infringement.

The Court also held that responses generated by ChatGPT using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) were not substantially similar to ANI’s original works and therefore did not infringe copyright.

The Court further observed that restraining OpenAI at this stage would cause irreparable injury not only to the company but also to the public at large.

The suit, filed by ANI in November 2024, is the first copyright action by an Indian news organisation against OpenAI.

ANI alleged that OpenAI had used its copyrighted news reports without permission to train ChatGPT and that the chatbot generated responses which copied or closely summarised its reports. It also claimed that ChatGPT falsely attributed fabricated news reports and statements to ANI, harming its reputation.

ANI, on October 3, 2024, offered to grant a license to OpenAI for using the news contents for the training of the LLM. However, the US-based company declined this proposal.

ANI’s counsel had, during the hearing, stated it is publicly known that OpenAI have entered into strategic partnerships and licensing arrangements with news organisations such as the Financial Times, Associated Press, and Conde Nast that function on a similar business model as ANI.

OpenAI has denied the allegations, maintaining that ANI’s website had been excluded from future training and that ChatGPT did not unlawfully reproduce ANI’s works.

World.title: Vijay’s CMO to be shifted to Namakkal Kavingar Maaligai due to space constraints
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), functioning out of the main block of Fort St. George in Chennai, will soon move to the 10th floor of Namakkal Kavignar Maaligai, amid reports in sections of the media that the State government is considering shifting the Secretariat from the Fort, Chennai’s prominent vestige of the colonial era, to another location.

At present, the 10th floor of Namakkal Kavignar Maaligai (also located in the premises of Fort St. George), is used for conferences, including those chaired by the Chief Minister with District Collectors and Superintendents of Police. Space constraints are cited as the primary reason for the shift. An official said that even after the CMO is relocated to the 10th floor, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay may occasionally use the existing Chief Minister’s chamber in the main block.

There have been reports that the site of the mofussil bus terminus in Koyambedu, now lying unutilised after the terminus was shifted to Kilambakkam, is being considered for housing the Secretariat. However, there is a view within the government that as Koyambedu is already congested, relocating the Secretariat there would only worsen the situation.

The Highways Research Station (HRS) campus, opposite Lok Bhavan in Guindy, is another site that has been occupying the attention of the government, including a couple of Ministers. Twenty-two years ago, when Jayalalithaa was Chief Minister, offices and educational institutions situated on the Anna University campus in Guindy, as well as nearby campuses such as the Madras School of Economics (MSE) and the HRS, were asked to shift elsewhere so that work on the new Secretariat complex at Kotturpuram could commence. The Research Station was even partially shifted to another site in Guindy. Eventually, the government abandoned the Kotturpuram project, enabling the HRS to return to its original site.

“As of now, it [the new venue for the Secretariat] is all in the realm of ideas,” observed an official.

World.title: Kerala BDS student death: HC slams police for failing to follow protocol in arrest of professor M.K. Ram
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has found that the grounds of arrest were not furnished to the accused, Dr. M.K. Ram, in the Kannur dental student death case when he was produced before the Special Judge the other day.

Dr. Ram, a former HoD, is the prime accused in the death of Nithin Raj, a first-year student of Kannur Dental College, Anjarakandy. Dr. Ram was charged with abetment to suicide and offences under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. He was denied bail at all levels, from the Special Court, Thalassery, to the Supreme Court.

The Single Bench of Justice A. Badharudeen, who called for the arrest details, observed that the guidelines issued by the Supreme Court requiring to provide written grounds of arrest was not given to Dr. Ram, which led to his release by the Special Court. This was affirmed by a report from the Additional Director General of Police, filed before the court on Friday (July 24, 2026).

The Crime Branch Deputy Superintendent of Police and the Superintendent of Police have appeared in person before the court to explain the sequence of events leading up to the arrest.

The court orally asked the DySP to explain why he had failed to comply with the requirements relating to the grounds of arrest, despite having made numerous arrests during his 22-year career as a police officer. The court also expressed its indignation to the SP for his lapse in ensuring that all arrest procedures were strictly followed in the arrest of Dr. Ram, as it was “an important matter concerning the State.”

The court orally remarked that as the Superintendent of Police, he must ensure that such errors shall not recur in such cases.

The court made the observations while considering a petition filed by the deceased student's father, alleging that he was not granted a chance to be heard when Mr. Ram had sought anticipatory bail before the Supreme Court. Instead of submitting to the process of law, Mr. Ram had deliberately absconded and evaded arrest, despite the knowledge of the criminal proceedings initiated against him.

Dr. Ram surrendered before the Crime Branch on Wednesday after the Special Court in Thalassery permitted his re-arrest.

The Home Department had reconstituted the investigation team that probed the case after the High Court had observed that serious allegations were raised against the earlier investigating officer. The investigation was handed over to Malappuram Crime Branch SP M.P. Mohanachandran, with DySP Jeevan George appointed as the new investigating officer.

World.title: How Kerala keeps its Karkkadakam rituals alive
World.content:
Karkkadakam was usually not the most desirable of months. It rained incessantly, there was sickness and scarcity, disease and death. When everything turned grey and gloomy, people devised ingenious ways to stay healthy and positive. They relied on belief and built rituals around them to help cope with the harshness of the season. While many of these rituals disappeared with time, a few still remain.

Theyyam for hope

In the northern regions of Kerala, from Kannur up to Kasaragod, Karkkadaka Theyyams appear, bringing with them a sense of hope and prosperity. In unrelenting rain, amid the beats of the chenda, these Theyyams arrive, singing the songs of the Gods. These are usually performed by children from the designated communities. Among the Karkkadaka Theyyams in Kasaragod region are the Aadi Galinchan, performed by the Nalkadaya community, the Karkkadothi Theyyam, performed by the Vannan community and the Aadi Vedan Theyyam performed by the Malaya community. In Kannur, Karkkadothi and Vedan and the two Theyyams that are performed during the month. Families offer rice and money to the performers.

“The belief is that they remove all the negativity surrounding the season, including diseases and death and ring in a sense of positivity. The reason why children are chosen is that their innocence is believed to bring in prosperity,” says Venugopal Panikker, a former English teacher and Theyyam performer from Kanayi, near Payyannur, Kannur.

It has a socio-economic aspect as well, adds Venugopal. “By May, the Theyyam season ends and and the artists have no work and means of income. This way, the families are able to tide over the difficult season,” he adds.

Leave, Chetta

Warding off chetta and welcoming Sheevothi is the most popular ritual, still practised in many parts of Kerala, with regional variations. On Karkkadakam eve, chetta or Jyestha Bhagavathy who stands for all things “dirty” is asked to leave and her younger sister, Sheevothi or Sree Bhagavathy who personifies prosperity, is welcomed in. The entire process resembles a performance of sorts. One of them being the practice of taking turmeric, charcoal, coconut shell, coconut fibre, broom, taro plant and soil from four corners of the house and placing them in a clay pot or a basket and discarding them while chanting ‘Chetta po... Sheevothivaa...’. This is both a call for the bad to leave and an invocation of the good. This is prevalent in parts of Palakkad district and north Malabar.

Here, on the first day of Karkkadakam, families perform Sheevothi vakkal, where a traditional lamp is lit and objects such as valkkannadi (traditional mirror) and dashapushpam (ten sacred flowers) are arranged. Holy texts are also kept, usually the Ramayana. Some even keep kajal, sindoor, turmeric, and a piece of sandal. Girls apply homemade mehndi on this day.

In parts of central and southern Kerala, warding off chetta is done on the last day of Karkkadakam so as to welcome the month of Chingam, the season of harvest. “When we were young, it was the senior most member of the family who used to do this. To welcome sheevothi we light the traditional lamp kept on a palaka (wooden pooja stool). Tulsi leaves and kindi (a type of pitcher with a sprouted aperture) filled with water are also kept. Back door is kept closed to keep chetta out,” says Remadevi P, a homemaker from Thiruvananthapuram, who has her roots in Kozhikode.

Alappuzha-native Rajasree Santhosh, now settled in Thiruvananthapuram, seconds this. “When you throw away the old things, you have to do that with your back turned,” Rajasree says. However, in some pockets of Thrissur, it is the youngest of the family who take out the discarded things in a clay pot placed on his head, saying ‘Pottiyum makkalum po po, Deviyum makkalum va va...’,” she says.

Appeasing Kaliyan

Another interesting ritual is Kaliyanu kodukkal, which is meant to appease the figure called Kaliyan, a mythical figure who is believed to ensure a good harvest. “The mango and jackfruit seasons are over by the time Karkkadakam begins. Since it is believed to be a month of scarcity and diseases owing to the rain, we exhort Kaliyan to ensure enough produce,” says young folk musician, Athul Narukara, who recently posted a Reel on his social media page about the ritual at his home at Manjeri in Malappuram district.

The midrib of banana leaves are cut in the shape of a little ladders and stairs. “We make the shape of a kaala (ox) from jackfruit leaves. A choottu (torch made with dried coconut leaves) is lit and all these are taken outside the house; homemade food is served in a coconut shell for Kaliyan. We keep chanting lines asking Kaliyan to bless us with a good harvest, and howl at the top of our voice. We had so much fun doing so. The practice, however, is slowly dying down,” says Athul, adding, “Another ritual is that my mother would pluck a taro plant (chembu) from the soil and hurl it on to the roof the house, standing with her back towards the house.”

Models of other agricultural equipment are also placed. In some households, these items are kept under a jackfruit tree in the compound.

A musical ode to the season

Towards central Kerala, around Ernakulam and Kottayam regions, a musical ritual known as Raveli vayana (also known as Blaveli vayana) is performed during Kakkadakam. It is a form of musical narration of the story of Lord Siva, which the singer performs, pointing to an illustration or painting with a bamboo stick. The singers are usually from the Veerasaiva community, and they visit homes in the mornings where they are welcomed by the families with a lit lamp and are offered a small dakshina (offering). “The singers used to come during the rainy mornings of Karkkadakam and would be welcomed with a sense of reverence. Nowadays, the practice is not prevalent, as few from the community continue this,” says TR Premkumar, founder of Moozhikkulam Sala, a space dedicated to natural living.

A pookkalam in the rain

Although pookkalam or floral carpets are laid only on the 10 days leading up to Onam, which falls in Chingam, in parts of north Kerala, pookkalam or floral carpets are laid from Karkkadakam itself. Also, Thiruvonam star in the month of Karkkadakam is observed as Pilleronam, a mini Onam with a feast but sans pookkalam and new clothes.

Food for the season

Karkkadakam also exerts its influence on the food consumed. Besides the Karkkadaka kanji (a medicinal gruel), some consume medicinal balls made with fenugreek (uluva) on the first seven days. “Fried and powdered uluva is mixed with jaggery, coconut and a medicinal mix available in shops to make the balls, which you have to consume on an empty stomach in the morning,” says Ramani C, a homemaker from Irinjalakkuda. These days she purchases the same from a Kudumbasree unit, Surabhi, in her neighbourhood. Dinsha Ramesh, a member of the unit says, “We have been making it for five years now. We usually buy 50 kg of uluva and dry it in the sun. To this we add cumin, aashali (garden cress), sathakuppa (dil), sesame, ayamodakam (ajwain), dried ginger, jaggery and coconut.”

For Dr Arya Naveen, it is that time of the year to consume kodangal (Indian pennywort), a medicinal plant, which she says helps develop immunity and aids digestion. “Add crushed or ground kodangal leaves and pepper powder to four teaspoons of buttermilk. Have it on empty stomach, but only two or three teaspoons. My mother, at times, adds the leaves to breakfast dishes such as idli or dosa,” she says.

Eventhough many people abstain from non-vegetarian food this month, in certain parts of Palakkad, it is a norm to have dosa with a chicken curry that has ash gourd in it for breakfast!

For the Brahmin community in Kerala, Tuesdays and Fridays of the month are special. “While pongal and thalagam (a mixed vegetable spicy curry) are prepared on Tuesdays, payasam is the special on Fridays. On the 18th day, we cook different rice varieties. We don’t recite Ramayana, instead we pray to Devi during this month,” says Sreevidya K, a homemaker from Thiruvananthapuram.

World.title: Supreme Court bars posting, uploading court proceedings on social media without prior permission
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (July 24, 2026) barred posting, reposting or uploading of audio-video recordings of court proceedings on social media and other digital platforms without prior permission of the concerned secretary general of the apex court or the registrar generals of the high courts.

A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also sought responses from the Centre and others on a plea raising the misuse of live-streaming and circulation of videos of court proceedings on social media.

“As an interim measure, it is directed that there shall be no extraction, modification, dissemination… posting, reposting and uploading of audio-video visual recordings of judicial proceedings on social media or other digital platforms without prior permission of the secretary general of this court or the registrar general of the jurisdictional high courts,” the Bench said.

Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, highlighted the misuse of videos of court proceedings on social media and other digital platforms.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta agreed with Mr. Singh and said there has to be some regulation.

World.title: Assam woman dies after C-section, husband, daughters get Rs 40 lakh compensation
World.content:
The Assam State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held a medical clinic and a doctor liable for medical negligence and deficiency of service, directing them to pay Rs 40 lakh to the family of a woman who allegedly died of complications after undergoing a C-section surgery to give birth to her second child in 2010.

President Justice Malasri Nandi and members Chandan Das, Pratim Kumar Bora and Tapas Kumar Ghosh were hearing a plea filed by the husband and his two daughters against the clinic and the doctor, accusing them of medical negligence and deficiency of service which led to the death of the woman due to multi-organ failure.

Besides ordering a relief of nearly Rs 30 lakh, the commission held that “losing of mother by her children were hard enough. The husband also lost his wife. We therefore allow additional compensation of Rs 10,00,000 only to be paid to the complainants…as punitive damage along with cost of litigation amounting to Rs 20,000”.

The man alleged that his wife died on October 2, 2010, because of “gross” negligence and “recklessness” on the part of the clinic and the doctor which caused her to experience huge blood loss during the Caesarean section or C-section performed by the doctor. The blood loss allegedly led to systemic clotting, which did not allow blood flow to the organs and ultimately caused multi-organ failure.

He said his wife had conceived in February 2010 and used to visit the clinic and the doctor for regular consultation for her pregnancy. He added that her ultrasound reports indicated that the placenta, a foetal support organ, was attached to the front wall of the uterus and partially or completely covered the cervix.

The husband claimed that the condition, along with her medical history, would have normally led a doctor to conclude that this was a complication and the placenta, instead of detaching normally after childbirth, would remain firmly stuck, posing a major risk of life-threatening heavy bleeding. He, however, said that the clinic and the doctor failed to prepare for such expected complications during the delivery and did not take appropriate care or precautions.

Further, the husband claimed that as per the standard practice in surgical complications, the surgeon concerned must work closely with the anaesthetist regarding the number of units of blood required before the surgery, which is a minimum of four units. It came on record that despite being aware of his wife’s condition, the doctor advised her to get admitted to the clinic on September 30, 2010, for an immediate C-section surgery with just one unit of blood.



On October 1, 2010, the wife was operated upon, and suffered from excessive bleeding during the delivery, but the blood loss could not be controlled or replaced, he said. Another doctor was called in to surgically remove the entire uterus and the cervix. The husband alleged that the woman’s condition deteriorated and she was transferred to another hospital where she died. Later, he moved the consumer commission claiming a compensation of Rs 87 lakh.

‘No negligence’

Senior Advocate Z Kamar and advocate B Talukdar, appearing on behalf of the clinic and the doctor, argued that on September 30, after seeing the ultrasound report, the wife was advised to take immediate admission and undergo a C-section delivery. However, she did not admit herself immediately and came in the next morning.

The counsel claimed the couple was informed about the risk factors associated with the surgery, including the risk of hysterectomy and non-availability of the blood bank on the premises, apart from one unit of blood arranged before the surgery.

The counsel stated that considering the woman’s condition, all doctors who may have been required in the surgery were kept ready on call. It was claimed that the bleeding was fully under control after the hysterectomy and 10 units of blood were arranged without any delay.



The clinic claimed that the woman’s vitals were stable throughout the procedure. Later, because of continuous increased heart rate, she was transferred to another hospital where she developed blood clotting and multi-organ failure.

Appearing for the second hospital, advocate D Baruah stated that at the time of admission, the woman was bleeding profusely, and despite maximum medical support, blood transfusion and all possible emergency measures, she could not be revived. He said there was no negligence or service deficiency on the part of the doctors.

Advocate U J Saikia appeared for the husband and his daughters.

Bald denial: Commission

The state commission noted that though the clinic, the doctors and the hospital submitted their written statements in the matter, they failed to examine any witness or present any document to prove their defence. It stated that in the absence of any supporting evidence, “such bald denial by the opposite parties regarding medical negligence…cannot be accepted”.



Also Read | Police protection for criminal case accused sends wrong signal: Allahabad High Court

The commission observed that the woman was 36 years old at the time of her death and, according to the husband, she ran a business and submitted income tax returns. The commission said that even if she was only a homemaker, the clinic and doctor must pay compensation in the form of at least the minimum wages in Assam.

Assuming that “she would be able to work till the age of 60 years when she would reach the retirement age as per the government employees”, the clinic and the doctor should pay compensation of Rs 400 per day for 26 working days in a month for 24 years, amounting to Rs 29.95 lakh, it held.

They were also ordered to pay an additional compensation of Rs 10 lakh as “punitive damage” along with litigation costs of Rs 20,000. The amounts were directed to be paid in 60 days.

Takeaway

The ruling establishes the obligation of medical professionals to ensure proper treatment of their patients. It also emphasises that doctors must be prepared for foreseeable childbirth complications, and unsupported denials cannot defeat a medical negligence claim.



For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories (Assam: 1800-3453-611) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.

World.title: Bangladesh President Shahabuddin, close ally of Sheikh Hasina, likely to resign today
World.content:
Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin is expected to resign on Friday after informing Prime Minister Tarique Rahman of his decision, reports said. (File Photo)

Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin, a former ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, is expected to resign on Friday, as per a report by Reuters. This comes days after Sheikh Hasina said she intended to return home from exile and surrender.

A report by the Dhaka Tribune said President Mohammed Shahabuddin has expressed his intention to resign and the Bangladesh government has accepted his proposal, according to his Press Secretary Mohammad Sarwar Alam.

The development comes as Speaker of Parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmad cut short his visit to Thailand and is returning to Bangladesh earlier than scheduled.

Formal resignation expected soon

President Mohammed Shahabuddin gained prominence after the 2024 uprising forced former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to flee to India. Shahabuddin, 76, was elected unopposed in 2023 as the Awami League’s nominee. Sources told Reuters that he informed the Prime Minister Tarique Rehman about his intent of resignation on Tuesday, with a formal announcement expected on Friday.

World.title: Sharmila Tagore on relationship lessons she learnt from Tiger Pataudi; an expert weighs in
World.content:
Sharmila Tagore has often spoken candidly about her marriage to the late Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi, fondly known as Tiger Pataudi. In a recent conversation with Barkha Dutt, the veteran actor reflected on the early years of their relationship, revealing that they chose to live together before marriage because it simply made practical sense. “We lived together before getting married because it was more convenient. Tiger would often go to the Cricket Club of India to shower because I was a terrible housekeeper. Nothing worked properly at home,” she said with a laugh. Looking back, she admitted, “I was a terrible housekeeper. I’ve learnt over the years. Now I’m very house-proud.”

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

The couple, who married in 1968 after several years of dating despite facing opposition and even death threats over their interfaith marriage, shared a relationship that lasted 43 years. Reflecting on what made their marriage endure in an earlier conversation with Tweak India, Sharmila said some of her greatest lessons came simply by observing her husband. “I was quite temperamental in those days, but I learnt a lot from Tiger. He was an extremely kind person. He would always say, ‘With dogs, with staff and with children, you must never raise your voice.'” She added, “He never really scolded me or put me down. Just by being there, he taught me patience and understanding.” One piece of advice, in particular, stayed with her throughout their marriage: “Words can be very vicious. Once spoken, you can’t take them back. You can be angry, you can disagree, but you shouldn’t say things that hurt each other because those words stay forever.” She has also previously shared that she knew he was the person she wanted to marry because of his sense of humour and because she instinctively felt “this man won’t hurt me on purpose.”

While every relationship is different, Sharmila’s reflections touch on themes many couples can relate to — learning from one another.

Accepting imperfections in long-term relationships

Dr Sakshi Mandhyan, psychologist and founder at Mandhyan Care, tells indianexpress.com, “Acceptance is one of the least understood aspects of long-term relationships. It does not mean agreeing with everything or tolerating unhealthy behaviour. It means recognising that every individual comes with strengths, limitations, habits, and emotional histories.”

In my work with couples, she says that she has found that people are far more willing to grow when they feel accepted rather than constantly corrected. “Many relationships become strained because partners spend years trying to reshape each other into an ideal version. Psychologically, acceptance creates emotional safety. Emotional safety allows people to be authentic, vulnerable, and also open to change.”

Patience is equally important because growth does not usually happen at the same pace for both partners.



Mutual respect helps couples hold differences without contempt or power struggles. “Most long-lasting couples I have worked with are not free of differences. What stands out is that they have learnt how to live with these variations without losing respect for each other,” notes Dr Mandhyan.

Is this healthy conflict or hurtful communication? Click each situation to see which approach helps protect trust during disagreements. Reacting immediately when emotions are high ❌ Strong emotions often make people say things they later regret. Taking a short pause before continuing the conversation can prevent lasting emotional damage. Talking about your own feelings instead of making accusations ✅ Saying ‘I felt hurt when…’ is usually more constructive than ‘You always…’ because it focuses on your experience rather than attacking your partner.

World.title: Saudi prince died at London hotel in 2025 after alcohol and drugs, coroner rules
World.content:
A photograph of Saudi prince Abdullah bin Fahad bin Abdula bin Jalawi Al Saud, who was found dead in a luxury hotel room at the Marriott Hotel in Kensington on November 25 last year, has surfaced for the first time.

The 29-year-old prince was found by a hotel cleaner in the bathroom of his locked fifth-floor room. He was fully clothed when he was discovered.



Hotel security staff and paramedics were called immediately, but despite repeated attempts to revive him, he was pronounced dead.

According to the Daily Mail, rooms at the hotel cost around 600 Euros per night.

A post-mortem examination concluded that the prince suffered a cardiac arrest after ingesting alcohol, the party drug gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB), and several other substances.

World.title: ‘Will take those extra miles’: Supreme Court to monitor NEET overhaul
World.content:
This comes a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the alleged NEET paper leaks issue, announcing fast-track courts to ensure speedy justice in such cases. (Representational Image/ PTI)

Amid the ongoing protest in Delhi against paper leaks, the Supreme Court said Friday it would closely monitor the Centre’s overhaul of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), cautioning that a shift to computer-based testing alone would not eliminate the risk of paper leaks.

The Centre, meanwhile, assured the court it was going “10 extra miles” to safeguard the NEET process.

A bench presided by Justice P S Narasimha and also comprising Justice Alok Aradhe was hearing pleas seeking reconstitution of the National Testing Agency (NTA) following the alleged NEET question paper leaks.

“We will monitor it, we will see. We will take those extra miles… We cannot let this go on… We will see that this is completely institutionalised and how it works, not just the commencement. We will follow it up throughout the year and see that complete and total institutionalisation takes place,” Justice Narasimha said.

World.title: Indian Railways provides two bed sheets in AC coaches, here’s why
World.content:
Indian Railways AC Coaches: Indian Railways provides two bed sheets to passengers travelling in AC coaches as part of its standard bedroll kit. The arrangement is meant to ensure better comfort, hygiene and convenience during overnight and long-distance journeys.

According to the Railway Board, the national transporter provides bedrolls to all passengers travelling in air-conditioned classes. The cost of the bedroll is included in the ticket fare for First AC, Second AC, Third AC and AC Economy passengers. Each bedroll packet contains two bed sheets, one pillow cover and a hand towel. But have you ever wondered why the national transporter gives passengers two bed sheets in AC coaches?



Why AC passengers get two bed sheets

In a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on Friday, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that one bed sheet is meant for keeping on sleeper seat, while the second bed sheet is intended to be used under the blanket. This prevents the blanket from coming into direct contact with the passenger’s body. “This blanket cover sheet is washed after single use,” Vaishnaw said.

The Union Minister was responding to questions raised by Rajya Sabha MP Chandrakant Damodar Handore, who sought details on the health and hygiene rationale behind washing woollen blankets only once a month while bed sheets are laundered after every journey.

He also asked about the status of mechanised and BOOT laundries using AI camera-based stain detection technology and Whito-Meters to monitor linen cleanliness, the reduction in the prescribed lifespan of linen to phase out worn-out bedding faster, and whether Indian Railways has directed that the extra bed sheet in every bedroll kit be used as a sanitary layer between passengers and the blanket.



Responding to the queries, Vaishnaw said that, as a pilot initiative to improve passenger comfort and hygiene, Indian Railways has started providing blanket covers to all AC class passengers on trains operated by the North Western Railway and on the newly launched Vande Bharat Sleeper train running between Kamakhya and Howrah.

Indian Railways uses AI cameras and Whito-Meters to check linen cleanliness

The Railway Minister further said that Whito-Meters are used at all mechanised laundries to check the cleanliness of linen. CCTV cameras have also been installed at laundries across the network to monitor laundry operations.

“Indian Railways has also initiated the pilot project of using automated AI-camera stain detection technology in laundries at Pune Division, Central Railway and Jaipur & Jodhpur division, North Western Railway for ascertaining the quality of washed linen,” he added.



When does Indian Railways replace bed sheets and blankets?

Vaishnaw further said that the prescribed lifespan of bed sheets, blankets and other linen items is fixed under existing Railway rules. He added that these norms are reviewed periodically based on their usage, condition and serviceability. “Linen items found unserviceable are withdrawn and replaced in accordance with the prescribed norms,” the Union Minister added.

World.title: ‘30 pellets still inside my body’: Journalist hurt in CJP protest seeks compensation
World.content:
Three days after the ‘Chalo Sansad’ march, the 28-year-old sports journalist with Outlook is back home in Delhi, working through the pain with more than 30 pellets still lodged inside his body.

A medical report issued by Safdarjung Hospital on July 22, reviewed by The Indian Express, records that he sustained injuries from “physical assault at Jantar Mantar by pellet gun”, with wounds over his right arm, chest, and back.

The hospital’s examination recorded small, punched-out wounds across his right arm, chest, and back, with doctors noting injuries “consistent with pellets”. Despite the injuries, the journalist has resumed working from home.

“The FIFA tournament got over on the 19th, and today (July 23) is the India-Zimbabwe cricket match, so I’ve been following that,” he says, adding that he is eager to return to covering sports.

On July 20, dressed in a black T-shirt, light brown trousers, and grey sports shoes, the 28-year-old parked his Pulsar motorcycle at B-Block in Connaught Place before joining the Cockroach Janta Party’s ‘Chalo Sansad’ march, demanding accountability from the Centre over exam paper leaks and Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.



“After they took away Sonam Wangchuk, that was the turning point for me,” he says.

As the march moved from Jantar Mantar towards the streets around Connaught Place, the 28-year-old says he remained with the crowd until clashes broke out around 4 pm. “Initially, the police were firing tear gas into the sky, but then I saw it being aimed towards the crowd. A person standing just ahead of me was hit barely one or two inches above his eye by what I believe was a tear gas shell,” he recalls.

He remembers people running. “Everything turned blurry. I could see men in khaki and blue uniforms. The next thing I saw was an officer aiming a gun at me. I turned and started running, but I felt a shot hit my back,” he says.



“At first I felt a tingling sensation. Then it felt like my back was on fire.”

He walked a short distance before sitting down. “Later I saw multiple wounds where blood had clotted,” he says.

‘Removing them could do more harm than good’

With police restricting movement around Connaught Place, the 28-year-old waited for nearly an hour before riding to a friend’s house. “When I reached, I checked my vest. It was drenched in blood,” he says. His friend photographed the wounds and uploaded the images to ChatGPT. “That’s when we first suspected they were pellet injuries,” he says.



Later that evening, he received a tetanus injection. “The pain was excruciating while sleeping,” he says.

The following evening, on July 21, the 28-year-old went to Safdarjung Hospital, reaching around 7 pm and remaining there until nearly 4 am the next morning.

“The doctors first cleaned the wounds and put me on an IV drip, which eased the pain. Several doctors examined me. After a CT scan, MRI and X-ray, they told me I had been hit by more than 30 pellets,” he said.

According to him, the treating doctors advised against surgically removing them. “They told me there were pellets in large quantities. I counted around 25 to 30 myself. The doctors said they would have to make incisions to remove them, and that removing them could do more harm than good. They said, ‘Let them remain inside’,” he says.



The doctors also told him he was fortunate the pellets had not lodged close to his bones, he says. “They said if they had been near the bones, I might not have been able to move my arm.”

For now, the 28-year-old has been advised to take medicines whenever the pain worsens. “Doctors said the wounds will heal, but the pellets may remain inside. I don’t know what happens after that,” he says.

He has a follow-up appointment with an orthopaedic specialist at Safdarjung Hospital, but said he also plans to seek a second opinion elsewhere. For his injuries, he added, he wants “compensation from the government”.

World.title: ‘Laapata’ Tejashwi? Jantar Mantar echo in Bihar, but RJD leader missing in action
World.content:
As the Opposition rallies behind the youth protesters at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, one of its leaders conspicuous by his absence has been Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) national working president Tejashwi Yadav.
